title: [Bugfix][MiniMax M3] Share target embeddings with MTP under PP
body:
MiniMax M3 MTP checkpoints can omit input embeddings. Under pipeline parallelism, the drafter runs on the final stage, where the target normally has no embedding to share.

This PR has mainly 2 fixes:

1. Public path: Add an opt-in `include_mtp` flag to `spec_decode_needs_target_embed`, allowing MTP targets to request input embeddings on the final PP stage. The default remains unchanged for existing callers.
2. M3 specific path: Enable this flag in the AMD/NVIDIA target models so the normal weight loader loads embeddings on the final stage. Record whether the MTP checkpoint loaded its own embeddings, allowing the existing shared loader to reuse target embeddings when absent and preserve distinct draft embeddings when present.

Target embeddings are provisioned before draft loading, so a draft with distinct embeddings may retain an extra target copy.

### Validation

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/worker tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py -q`: **18 passed** (CPU).
- `pre-commit run`: **passed**.

AI assistance: Codex assisted implementation and testing. Draft pending GPU validation and submitter line-by-line review/test rerun.

title: [CI] Split (H200 MIG 35GB / MI355) Multimodal Models (Standard) 4 into ViT CUDAGraph, Audio and Pooling + Other jobs
body:
## What

Split `(H200 MIG 35GB) Multimodal Models (Standard) 4` (and its MI355 mirror) into three named jobs — ViT CUDAGraph, Audio, and Pooling + Other — instead of routing four parallel indices through a `case` block. The nine ViT cudagraph family wrappers move into `standard/vit_cudagraph/`, which makes them one whole coverage unit a named job can hash-shard directly.

## Old

```text
standard/
├── test_vit_cudagraph_{qwen,minicpmv,gemma4,llama4,kimi_vl,internvl,idefics3,glm4_1v,deepseek_ocr}.py
├── _vit_cudagraph.py
└── test_{gemma_ragged_audio,interleaved,mapping,memory_leak,whisper}.py  audio/  pooling/

one job, key multi-modal-models-standard-4-other-whisper, parallelism: 4,
`case "$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB"` hand-assigning files to indices
```

## New

```text
standard/
├── vit_cudagraph/
│   ├── _vit_cudagraph.py            # shared, not collected
│   └── test_{qwen,minicpmv,gemma4,llama4,kimi_vl,internvl,idefics3,glm4_1v,deepseek_ocr}.py
├── test_vit_cudagraph_eonly.py      # encoder-only (#56922); separate pytest process
├── audio/                           # gemma_ragged_audio, moss_audio, voxtral
├── pooling/
└── test_{interleaved,mapping,memory_leak,whisper}.py
```

| Job | Key | Replicas | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Standard 4: ViT CUDAGraph Shard %N` | `multi-modal-models-standard-4-vit-cudagraph` | 3 | `pytest standard/vit_cudagraph --num-shards --shard-id`; then `test_vit_cudagraph_eonly.py` in its own process on shard 0 only |
| `Standard 4: Audio` | `multi-modal-models-standard-4-audio` | 1 | `pytest standard/audio`; spawn-mode `pytest standard/test_whisper.py` from the repo root |
| `Standard 4: Pooling + Other` | `multi-modal-models-standard-4-pooling-other` | 1 | `pytest standard/pooling test_interleaved.py test_mapping.py`; `pytest test_memory_leak.py` |

Old key `multi-modal-models-standard-4-other-whisper` → `-audio` + `-pooling-other`. Each job keeps an inline `mirror.amd` block (generated `amd-<key>`). The MI355 legacy copy in `test-amd.yaml` follows the same three-way split.

## Notes

- `-m core_model` is dropped as redundant, not narrowed. Every `core_model` file outside `standard/` was already ignored by the old command, and the 14 core ViT model IDs are claimed exactly once across the nine wrappers (checked statically).
- **Exception to "side-effect tests get their own job":** `test_eonly_vit_cudagraph_outputs` monkeypatches the V2 runner and insecure serialization, and ViT cases that follow it in the same process segfault. It stays outside the hash-sharded folder and runs as a separate pytest process pinned to shard 0, so it always gets a fresh process. It doesn't get its own job because it requires CUDA, so all three AMD copies of a dedicated job would collect two tests and skip both. Say so if you would still rather it had its own job.
- Whisper stays outside `audio/` because it needs spawn from the repo root. Running it inside the folder would put it in-process, and excluding it would need an `--ignore`.
- Top of the stack: #57065 and #56901 → #57066 → this PR. Review only the last five commits here, from "Split Standard 4 into named…" onward. One scoped build on this head validates the whole stack. Rebased onto current `main`; `main`'s newer ViT configs (DeepSeek-V4.1, video metadata) are carried into the shared helper. AI assistance was used.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Labelled predictions. The ViT rows come from build 89163 (same 28-case directory, three-way hash). The two non-ViT rows split one previously measured bundle, which ran 16–18m pytest with no margin against the per-job target. How that bundle divides between Audio and Pooling + Other has not been measured.

| Job / replica | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| ViT CUDAGraph 1–3/3 | ~4–13m each | ~6–15m | ~1–2m | checkout + image pull |
| Audio | unmeasured (share of 16–18m) | — | ~1–2m | checkout + image pull, two pytest starts |
| Pooling + Other | unmeasured (share of 16–18m) | — | ~1–2m | checkout + image pull, two pytest starts |

Five workers replace the old job's four. The added cost is one extra worker's setup, about 1–2 worker-minutes, which is well inside the 20-minute aggregate budget. Every job is expected to stay under the 20-minute runtime target, because the old bundle is now split across two jobs. Measurements from build 91132 follow in a validation comment.

title: [ROCm][Attention] Window-aware split-KV gate and occupancy-aware launch config for Triton DiffKV
body:
## Purpose

Two launcher fixes for the Triton DiffKV attention kernel. The kernel itself is unchanged, and both are gated to gfx950, so gfx942 and all NVIDIA parts take the unmodified path.

Measured on MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, 4x MI350X, 8192 in / 1024 out / 32 concurrent:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Time per output token | 28.69 ms | **25.86 ms** |
| Time to first token | 2971 ms | **2675 ms** |
| Throughput | 9107 tok/s | **10104 tok/s** |

About 11% more throughput, GSM8K unchanged at 0.9844.

## Fix 1: the split-KV decision ignores the sliding window

The code picks between walking the KV cache in one pass and splitting it into 16 chunks computed in parallel, then stitched back together by a second kernel. It decides by asking whether there are enough sequences to keep the GPU busy without splitting. It never asks how much KV there is to walk.

With a sliding window those differ a lot. A window of 128 means only ~8 tiles of real work per sequence, not the 544 the sequence length implies. Split across 16 chunks, most chunks get nothing, yet the first kernel still writes 16 sets of partials and the stitching kernel still reads all 16 back. Counters confirm it: that second kernel does zero matrix math and moves 6.5 GB purely to undo a split that bought nothing.

The fix also checks the window is large enough to be worth splitting. Decode, 32 sequences:

- sliding-window layers: 17.5 us not splitting vs 34.2 us splitting
- full-attention layers: 168 us splitting vs 424 us not, so splitting must stay

That second row is why the fix is conditional. Disabling the split everywhere was 42% slower.

The cutoff works out to ~256 KV tokens per chunk, stable across 2/4/8 KV heads and batch 8/32/64. The mechanism is not AMD-specific but that constant was only measured on gfx950, hence the arch gate. Widening it is a follow-up.

## Fix 2: the launcher never told Triton how to run the kernel

No `num_warps` or `num_stages` were passed, so Triton used its default of 4 warps. The query block here is small, so at 4 warps each gets a few rows and every softmax step crosses local memory. One warp keeps it in registers and cuts local memory use by a third.

Keying this off whether we split turns out to be wrong. Two cases compile to a byte-identical kernel, both non-splitting, yet one warp is 1.48x faster in one and 0.88x slower in the other. The only difference is GPU occupancy: 64 workgroups per compute unit vs 0.5.

So the check is on occupancy. Threshold is 8 workgroups per compute unit: one warp per workgroup, 4 SIMDs per CU, so 8 gives 2 warps per SIMD, the minimum for one to cover another's latency. It started at 4 and was raised because results in the 4-5 range would not reproduce, coming back as both a 1.5x win and a 0.55x loss.

The splitting path gets no occupancy check. Measured across 42 configurations it does not depend on occupancy, because its pipelining hides latency inside the warp. Gating it too would have lost a 1.22x win.

Per model step across all 70 layers: prefill 61951 to 39643 us, decode 3691 to 2413 us.

## Test plan

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 128 --num-warmups 32 --seed 4

lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --apply_chat_template --num_fewshot 5 --limit 64
```

## Test result

**Correctness.** Fix 2 changes only how the kernel is launched, so output is exactly identical, asserted as a difference of 0.0 rather than a tolerance. Fix 1 changes which path runs, reordering some floating point additions: 3.9e-03 against a full precision reference, well inside bf16 tolerance.

**Regressions.** 99 configurations across 3 head layouts, 4 batch sizes, 3 window sizes, both paths. Zero regressions: the 42 cases where the occupancy rule declines come back at exactly 1.000x, and all 15 where it fires are between 1.08x and 1.70x faster.

**Arch gating.** Verified by stubbing the device probe. gfx942 and an NVIDIA part take the unmodified path for every window size and grid shape tested; gfx950 reproduces the benchmarked build exactly.

**Accuracy.** GSM8K 5-shot 0.9844, same as baseline.

**End to end.** Two runs per arm. Time per output token was 28.59 and 28.79 before, 25.98 and 25.74 after. Spread under 1%, so 11% is well clear of noise.

Measured on vLLM e97573215, AITER built from source a75ba53de, ROCm 7.2.3.

## Not duplicating existing work

No open PR touches `triton_unified_attention_diffkv.py`. Three are adjacent, all on the non-DiffKV kernel:

- **#47520** derives the split-KV threshold from compute unit count. Closest existing work, and Fix 2 shares its spirit that the heuristic ignores the hardware. Still different: #47520 makes the decision device-aware, this makes it window-aware, and its diff never looks at the window.
- **#58482** raises chunk count 16 to 64 when the GPU would idle, on SM120. That adds chunks where there is work to spread; this removes the split where chunks would be empty.
- **#45450** admits sliding-window layers to the split path, but only under speculative decoding and on the non-DiffKV kernel. Neither applies here.

## Scope and limits

Only gfx950 is affected. This file is also only reached by models whose value head dimension differs from the key head dimension, so equal-head-dim models are untouched regardless.

The constants, 256 KV tokens per chunk and 8 workgroups per compute unit, were measured on MI350X and are tied to the current tile and chunk sizes, which is why the arch gate is there.

One model at one shape. The same window-blind decision exists in the non-DiffKV `triton_unified_attention.py`, so other sliding-window models are probably paying the same cost. Untested, untouched here.

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Frontend][Rust][Multimodal] Add Gemma 4 image support / multimodal model spec
body:
## Purpose
Fixes #58580

This PR adds Gemma 4 multimodal model processor specification and vision preprocessor support to the Rust frontend (`vllm-chat`).

### Changes
1. **Aspect-Ratio-Preserving Size Calculation**: Implements `get_aspect_ratio_preserving_size` and `compute_num_soft_tokens` matching the Gemma 4 vision encoder geometry (`patch_size`, `pooling_kernel_size`, `max_soft_tokens`).
2. **Gemma 4 Vision Preprocessor**: Implements `Gemma4VisionProcessor` adhering to the vision tower input schema (`pixel_values` of shape `[batch, max_patches, patch_pixels]` with zero-padding and `pixel_position_ids` with `(col, row)` coordinates and `(-1, -1)` for padding patches).
3. **Dynamic Prompt Replacement**: Generates dynamic image placeholder expansions (`[boi_token_id] + [image_token_id; num_soft_tokens] + [eoi_token_id]`) where only `image_token_id` soft tokens are marked for embedding substitution.
4. **Registry Fallback**: Wires `Gemma4Spec` as an in-tree fallback in `resolve_model_spec` so that `gemma4` and `gemma4_unified` models resolve their multimodal spec directly in the Rust frontend.

title: [MM][Mistral] Add compile support for Pixtral vision encoders
body:
## Purpose
Add `compile_mm_encoder` support for both Pixtral vision encoder implementations:

- `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`, including Mistral-format Mistral 3 models.
- The Hugging Face Pixtral encoder used by `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`.

The change applies `support_torch_compile` to the transformer blocks in both implementations and marks the token, rotary embedding, and packed-sequence dimensions as dynamic.

The feature remains gated behind `compile_mm_encoder`, which is disabled by default.

### Performance results
Note: the results are only about GPU kernel time. Total E2E runtime improves much less, even with Cuda graphs from #56277, because apply_hf_processor is the main bottleneck now.

Profiling was performed on an NVIDIA GB200 system using the same 16-image BF16 capture before and after enabling compilation. 
Total GPU kernel time decreased by **42%**, from **1173.6 ms to 676.8 ms**, corresponding to a **1.73x speedup**.

The improvement came from eliminating or fusing much of execution overhead:

| Kernel category | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FlashAttention | 273 ms | 273 ms | 0% |
| GEMM | 272 ms | 272 ms | 0% |
| Elementwise operations | 368 ms | 11 ms | 97% |
| SiLU | 121 ms | 44 ms | 64% |
| Concat | 96 ms | 0.3 ms | >99% |


  ### CUDA-graph compatibility

  This work is complementary to #56277, which adds Pixtral encoder CUDA-graph support. It does not duplicate or modify that implementation.

  The CUDA-graph PR’s pixtral.py and mistral3.py changes apply cleanly over this change. Its packed encoder forwards continue to use the unchanged transformer interface. Encoder CUDA-graph capture also performs an eager warmup before capture,
  allowing the transformer blocks to compile first.

  A combined compile_mm_encoder=True plus cudagraph_mm_encoder=True integration test should be added once #56277 is merged.

## Test Plan
Exercise both encoder implementations with compilation enabled and disabled:

- Mistral-format `PixtralForConditionalGeneration`
- Hugging Face `Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration`

The test uses dummy weights and verifies that the compilation counter increases only when `compile_mm_encoder` is enabled.

## Test Result

```console

  tests/compile/fullgraph/test_multimodal_compile.py \
  -k pixtral_compilation -vv -s

4 passed, 4 deselected
```

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Fuse small-batch WO-A with inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant on SM100/SM103
body:
## Purpose

On SM100/SM103, the DSv4.1 O-projection runs four kernels per layer: Triton inverse RoPE with per-32 FP8 quant, DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum` for the grouped `wo_a`, a FlashInfer MXFP8 quantize, and the FlashInfer CuTe-DSL `wo_b` GEMM. At decode batch sizes the first three are latency-bound and together take 11-12 µs on GB200 (DSv4.1-Flash, TP=4).

This PR adds `FusedWoAKernel`, a CuTe-DSL kernel that replaces those three and hands `wo_b` a pre-quantized `QuantizedActivation`:

- 128 CTAs in clusters of 8. Each cluster owns 128 `wo_a` output rows, and each CTA owns one head (512 of K = 4096) and TMA-prefetches its 64 KiB weight slice before `griddepcontrol.wait`, overlapping the previous kernel under PDL.
- Inverse RoPE and per-32 UE8M0 quantization of the attention output go straight into the swizzled SMEM operand; `tcgen05` block-scaled MMA accumulates in TMEM.
- Split-K partials are reduced over DSMEM, rounded to BF16 like the unfused path, and quantized to MXFP8 in FlashInfer's F8_128x4 scale layout, including the zero padding FlashInfer's quantizer writes.

`dsv41_o_proj(layer, attn_out, positions)`, which the FlashMLA and FlashInfer backends now call directly, takes the fused path for 1-32 tokens (the kernel's limit) on SM100/SM103 with 16 local heads in 2 groups (DSv4.1-Flash at TP=4), a per-32 FP8 `wo_a` with TMA-aligned scales, and a FlashInfer CuTe-DSL MXFP8 `wo_b`. Everything else stays on `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`.

The kernel follows the `VllmCuTeDSLJitKernel` warmup contract. The FlashMLA and FlashInfer SM100/SM103 backends register it at construction, and warmup compiles all 32 token counts (13.5 s on GB200): target graphs, DSpark draft graphs and eager batches land on different counts, so covering the whole range keeps runtime compile-free. `_wo_b_proj` keeps pre-quantized activations off GEMM-RS, which only runs from 128 tokens.

The kernel binds `amax`, `exponent` and `inv` before its output stage. vLLM imports `quack`, which rewrites `if const_expr(S) or D:` process-wide into a constexpr if; without the binding, token counts whose input stage takes the dynamic path (3, 5, 6, 7, 9, ...) fail warmup with `TYPE_UNSTABLE_JOIN` inside a server even though they compile in isolation.

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `wo_a`, `fused wo_a`, `DSv4.1 o_proj`, `inverse RoPE MXFP8`, `fused_inv_rope` and `o_proj cutedsl`. #57977 (draft) also targets the `wo_a` to `wo_b` handoff, but keeps `fp8_einsum`, has it emit MXFP8, and moves `wo_b` to DeepGEMM; this PR instead collapses the whole pre-`wo_b` chain into one kernel for small batches. Both touch the same call sites; if #57977 lands first, the fused kernel could emit DeepGEMM's packed scale layout for that `wo_b` instead. #58621 changes DSv4, not DSv4.1.

## Validation

The fused kernel should cut decode latency at small batch sizes without changing what the model produces. The checks below compare this branch (`f6f4b68630`; the later head only edits docstrings) against its merge-base with main (`e33de821c0`), with everything else held fixed.

### Setup

- **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.7.0, CuTe DSL 4.7.1; both sides share one venv built from the merge-base's precompiled wheel and the same kernel caches.
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`).
- **Topology:** TP4 (no expert parallel), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` attention.

### Kernel microbenchmark

DSv4.1-Flash TP=4 shapes (16 local heads, FP8 `wo_a` [2, 1024, 4096], MXFP8 `wo_b` [5120, 2048]). Both paths run through their production entry points with the libraries' default PDL settings. Timing is the CUPTI span from first kernel start to last kernel end, with CUDA graphs and cold L2, median of 7 rotated rounds x 500 iterations. O-proj includes the `wo_b` GEMM; WO-A is the part the fused kernel replaces.

| Tokens | O-proj (µs) | Speedup | WO-A (µs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 16.13 → 10.37 | 1.56x | 11.17 → 5.79 | 1.93x |
| 4 | 17.09 → 10.59 | 1.61x | 11.52 → 6.14 | 1.88x |
| 8 | 16.69 → 11.26 | 1.48x | 11.52 → 6.69 | 1.72x |
| 16 | 17.20 → 12.51 | 1.37x | 11.68 → 8.03 | 1.45x |
| 24 | 17.38 → 14.30 | 1.22x | 12.06 → 9.70 | 1.24x |
| 32 | 17.22 → 16.22 | 1.06x | 12.13 → 11.46 | 1.06x |

### Serving benchmark

TP4 without speculative decoding, random dataset with 8,192 input / 1,024 output tokens (range ratio 0, `ignore_eos`), prefix caching off, `4 × concurrency` prompts (at least 8). Both sides run in one job on one node after a warmup pass at every concurrency; each point is the median of 3 repeats with unique seeds, and no timed run triggered a JIT compile or a new DeepGEMM cache entry.

| Concurrency | ITL p50 (ms) | TPOT p50 (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) | TTFT p50 (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.37 → 4.14 (−5.3%) | 4.36 → 4.13 (−5.2%) | 218.6 → 230.6 (+5.5%) | 207 → 205 |
| 4 | 5.16 → 4.85 (−5.9%) | 5.23 → 4.89 (−6.5%) | 698.7 → 742.6 (+6.3%) | 510 → 509 |
| 8 | 5.73 → 5.48 (−4.4%) | 5.93 → 5.67 (−4.4%) | 1192.9 → 1241.6 (+4.1%) | 805 → 797 |
| 32 | 9.09 → 8.97 (−1.3%) | 11.28 → 11.07 (−1.9%) | 2523.0 → 2551.3 (+1.1%) | 1402 → 1420 |
| 64 | 11.28 → 11.31 (+0.3%) | 16.89 → 16.97 (+0.5%) | 3494.4 → 3486.8 (−0.2%) | 1409 → 1409 |

- Repeat spread is at most 0.03 ms in ITL p50 up to concurrency 32, so every gain there is well outside the noise.
- The gain shrinks with batch size as in the microbenchmark. Concurrency 64 exceeds the fused kernel's 32-token limit, stays on `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`, and is unchanged, as expected.
- TTFT stays within ±1.3%: prefill does not take the fused path.

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark configuration</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 256 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 131072 \
  --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --numa-bind --numa-bind-nodes 0 0 1 1

vllm bench serve --backend vllm --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|4|8|32|64>
```

</details>

### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy

Each run uses the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction, served with the benchmark configuration above. Each server runs the set twice. DSpark uses 5 speculative tokens, and acceptance is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over each run.

| Configuration | GSM8K strict (run 1 / run 2) | Acceptance length, incl. bonus |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base, DSpark | 93.03% / 92.57% | 3.470 / 3.473 |
| PR, DSpark | 93.03% / 93.33% | 3.469 / 3.477 |
| PR, no speculative decoding | 93.03% / 92.42% | - |

- Acceptance matches within 0.01 and the per-position curves coincide (run 1: base 0.796 / 0.655 / 0.462 / 0.341 / 0.217, PR 0.797 / 0.657 / 0.462 / 0.338 / 0.215).
- Every GSM8K score falls inside the 0.5-0.6 point spread between two repeats on the same server. These results establish parity with the base; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.

### GPQA Diamond

PR, TP4 without speculative decoding, `--max-model-len 1048576`; 198 problems, 0-shot chat completions, thinking on with the default (high) reasoning effort, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, 262,144-token output cap. Score **91.92%** from a single run (standard error about ±1.9 points); all 198 responses finished with `stop`, with a median of 2,134 and a maximum of 53,922 completion tokens.

### Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py -q
```

106 passed, both as is and with quack's preprocessor patch active (`-p quack.dsl`). The new test checks the fused kernel against the unfused Triton + DeepGEMM + FlashInfer reference at T in {1, 3, 6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 32} (every guard and tile size), with padded and unpadded attention output and all-zero input, under CUDA graph replay, including the scale padding. The fused FP8 data and scales are bit-identical to the unfused path in most cases; otherwise split-K accumulation order flips rare values (relative L2 up to 6.7e-4 after `wo_b`).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change: the implementation, the evaluation runs, and this description were produced with Claude Code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Treat padded prompt tails as spec-decode rows for hybrid models
body:
The scheduler pads a one-token prompt tail over prior state (e.g. a P/D decode-node arrival) with K placeholder drafts to keep the K+1 spec-decode shape (#45237). For recurrent-state layers these rows must run the spec-decode kernels, which keep the running state and roll the rejected placeholders back; the prefill kernels store only the state after all K+1 tokens (#55178).

#52988 changed the hybrid model state to classify spec-decode rows by request state (not prefilling) instead of num_scheduled_tokens, which adaptive verification rewrites. That sent every padded tail's draft count to -1, so Mamba's padded-tail handling no longer fires and GDN/KDA build the row as a prefill, folding the placeholder tokens into the request's recurrent state.

Also count prefilling rows with exactly one remaining prompt token and prior state as decodes, still using request state only.

title: [Qwen4Exp] support Sequence Parallelism for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
body:
## Purpose

Add sequence parallelism (SP) to Qwen4Exp / Qwen3.8-Flash-Next to reduce replicated GR and PLE computation and support sequence-parallel MoE.

- Enable GR/PLE SP with `--enable-hc-sp` while retaining tensor-parallel MoE.
- Automatically enable model SP with the existing sequence-parallel MoE configuration (`TP>1`, `DP>1`, EP enabled, and a supported all-to-all backend).

SP currently requires PP=1 and MoE layers. External LoRA adapters on SP-sharded GR/PLE projections are not supported.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_tpsp.py
```

## Test Results

- Regression tests: **92 passed**, including two-GPU GR/PLE SP and four-GPU MoE SP tests.
- Ruff and `git diff --check`: passed.

### Accuracy

Models: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` and its `-FP8` variant. MTP=3, PP=1, prefix caching disabled. Same prompts and generation settings within each pair: seed=1236, temperature=0.7, top_p=0.8, top_k=20, max_tokens=32768, thinking enabled.

Selected results, **SP off → on**. GSM8K: 1,319 questions; GPQA Diamond: 198 questions. Original evaluation scores are retained.

| Weights | Parallel configuration | PLE storage | GSM8K | GPQA Diamond |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 | TP2, ETP2 | CPU offload | 97.88% → 97.80% | 87.88% → 88.38% |
| BF16 | DP2/TP2/EP4, ETP4 | CPU offload | 98.10% → 98.03% | 87.88% → 85.35% |
| FP8 | DP2/TP2/EP4, ETP2 | GPU | 98.03% → 98.03% | 87.37% → 87.88% |

The SP-off EP baseline disables automatic MoE SP through a test-only override, keeping TP/DP/EP unchanged.

### Performance

BF16, PLE CPU offload, MTP=3, prefix caching disabled. Median of three runs; **SP off → on**.

Prefill: 8K/16K input, 1 output token, concurrency 2, 48 requests. Decode: 1 input token, 1,024 output tokens, concurrency 32, 128 requests. Synthetic random-token inputs; EP uses `allgather_reducescatter`.

| Parallel configuration | SP comparison | 8K TTFT (ms) | 16K TTFT (ms) | C32 TPOT (ms) | C32 output TPS (tok/s) | Improvement (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2, ETP2 | Off → On (level 1: GR/PLE) | 301.80 → 278.54 | 612.84 → 565.00 | 16.57 → 16.70 | 1925.64 → 1910.64 | +7.71 / +7.81 / -0.81 / -0.78 |
| DP2/TP2/EP4, ETP4 | Off → On (level 2: GR/PLE + MoE) | 311.64 → 313.95 | 455.12 → 418.47 | 19.35 → 19.49 | 1649.25 → 1629.42 | -0.74 / +8.05 / -0.75 / -1.20 |
| DP2/TP2/EP4, ETP2 | Off → On (level 2: GR/PLE + MoE) | 323.04 → 296.04 | 480.86 → 465.85 | 18.15 → 16.11 | 1707.45 → 1978.78 | +8.36 / +3.12 / +11.22 / +15.89 |

TP2 prefill improves by about 8%.  With DP2/TP2/EP4 and ETP2, C32 TPOT improves by 11.2%; decode does not improve in the other two configurations. DP scheduling contributes to run-to-run variation. Median MTP acceptance is approximately 0–0.15% at C32, so these decode results represent a low-acceptance workload.

> Cxx: denotes xx concurrent requests across the entire service

## Related PRs

Builds on #54371's PLE offload and ETP support, adding model SP. Open PR searches for `Qwen4Exp SP` and `Qwen4Exp "sequence parallel"` found no matching implementation on 2026-09-12.

title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Shard long-context indexer prefill rows across TP
body:
## TL;DR

**How it works / why it is faster:** Instead of repeating sparse-indexer prefill MQA scoring and top-k on every TP rank, partition independent query rows into cost-balanced contiguous slices. Each rank scores its rows against the full available key history; `all_gatherv` reassembles the final int32 indices. This removes redundant computation in exchange for fixed-width index communication, so savings grow with context length. There is no attention approximation. Decode kernels are unchanged; smaller batches retain the existing path (activation requires at least `16,384 × TP` scheduled prefill query rows).

**Performance, baseline → optimized:** main parent `5893426b88f7` → PR head `16934c6e76e5`; GLM-5.3-Flash on 4× H200, TP4, C1, 256 output tokens, 65,536-token batch budget, legacy runner + explicit FA3 backend. Four fresh-process A/B pairs in ABBA/BAAB order; warmups excluded. Throughput below counts input + output tokens at C1, **not saturated serving throughput**.

| Input context | Server TTFT, seconds (B → O) | TTFT reduction | Total tok/s (B → O) | Throughput increase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | 4.782 → 4.605 | 3.69% | 20,269.73 → 20,835.80 | 2.79% |
| 256K | 10.154 → 9.372 | 7.70% | 22,090.93 → 23,651.89 | 7.07% |
| 512K | 22.760 → 19.418 | 14.68% | 21,379.03 → 24,752.65 | 15.78% |
| 1M (1,000,000) | 54.154 → 40.388 | 25.42% | 17,856.28 → 23,675.18 | 32.59% |

Server-side TPOT at 1M: **6.631 → 6.633 ms/token**. Across the full 1K–1M scan, absolute TPOT percentage-change point estimates are <0.04%; every paired 95% interval includes zero. This does not prove equivalence. The 2K TTFT point estimate is 2.84% slower (interval crosses zero); we do not claim blanket short-input non-regression.

**Correctness / targeted accuracy, baseline → optimized:** Across 33 distinct retrieval probes spanning 1K–1M, repeated over four processes per arm, expected-answer presence is **132/132 → 132/132**; strict answer-only accuracy is **127/132 → 129/132**. Exact generated-token agreement is **130/132 A/B** (baseline A/A: **98/99**). Both observed A/B differences contain the same correct code, with an additional explanatory sentence in baseline. These are targeted retrieval checks, not a broad quality benchmark or a claim of bitwise equivalence. The 54 focused PR tests also pass.

Full eleven-length results, paired confidence intervals, implementation scope, and reproducibility details follow.

## Summary

Shard replicated sparse-indexer **prefill query rows** across tensor-parallel ranks. Each rank computes MQA logits and top-k for a cost-balanced contiguous slice, then one variable-size `all_gatherv` call per indexer layer restores the original row layout. This removes redundant scoring; it does not approximate attention or merge independent top-k candidates. The API call is not a claim of one underlying physical NCCL operation.

For GLM-5.3-Flash, the exchange includes the incomplete k-pool tail: `index_topk + index_kpool - 1 = 2,051` int32 columns. KV gathering remains unconditional because subsequent query chunks can reuse that workspace.

The avoided MQA scoring work grows with both query rows and the available pooled-key history, whereas the exchanged index width per query row stays fixed. Longer histories therefore offer more computation to save per byte exchanged. The cost-balanced partition also accounts for different causal-history lengths across rows. This targets prefill TTFT and prefill-dominated total-token throughput; the row partition and exchange are outside the decode branch, so a direct decode-kernel speedup is not expected. Indirect TPOT changes are measured and reported below.

## Scope and activation

The diff against main is four files: the shared DSA indexer metadata/planner, the generic sparse indexer, the GLM k-pool indexer, and their focused tests. #53906 is already in the baseline; this PR does not reintroduce its model support or kernel changes.

- Requires CUDA, TP > 1, an MQA prefill, and **at least `16,384 × TP` scheduled prefill query rows in the current batch**.
- DCP/PCP, non-CUDA platforms, disabled PyNCCL, NCCL symmetric-memory, batch-invariant mode, and configurations whose mixed CUDA-graph mode is FULL retain the existing path.
- Decode kernels, model weights, sampling, KV-cache format, and attention's mathematical definition are not changed. TPOT is nevertheless measured to check for indirect effects.
- The shared generic DSA path is also modified. H200 serving results below cover GLM-5.3-Flash only; they are not an end-to-end no-regression guarantee for other models, platforms, concurrency levels, or speculative decoding.

**Important configuration constraint:** at TP4, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` cannot activate this implementation, even with a 1M-token accumulated context. Both arms below use **65,536**, so C1 inputs of 1K–32K exercise the fallback, and full 64K prefill chunks can exercise sharding. The gate is a batch-row count, not the request's context length; several shorter concurrent requests can also reach it.

## Exact-head A/B rescan

These measurements replace the previous historical tables. Those tables used older PR/runtime overlays and an 8,192-token batch budget; their gains cannot be attributed to the current head and gate.

| Arm | Source commit |
|---|---|
| Baseline | main at `5893426b88f7b3cd21101d194eb1c6f0a6f0e27b`, the optimized commit's parent |
| Optimized | `16934c6e76e508b22037d5d4040488d490090044` |

Both arms load their respective clean source trees, the same model snapshot (`3f1971b7b5f7a528c9c4ef6212c8785298a8c24a`), and identical compiled vLLM extensions from the official wheel for the baseline commit. Worker-level provenance checks verify the loaded vLLM paths for all four TP ranks. The historical vendor-vLLM Python overlay is not used. The PR range contains one commit.

### Configuration and stability protocol

- 4 × NVIDIA H200, TP4, native FP8 weights, BF16 KV cache; text-only, **legacy model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0`) and explicit `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` attention backend**, chunked prefill, `max_model_len=1,048,576`, `max_num_batched_tokens=65,536`, `max_num_seqs=8`, GPU-memory utilization 0.90.
- MTP/speculative decoding off; prefix caching off; `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA-graph configuration with main's default breakable-graph behavior. The effective engine configuration reports `CompilationMode.NONE` and CUDA-graph capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`; this is not a torch.compile-enabled prefill benchmark. Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Transformers 5.12.1. Same process environment/cache policy in both arms; OMP/MKL threads fixed at 1. Synchronous CUDA debugging is off for timed runs. These explicit runner/backend settings avoid failures observed in the unmodified baseline; see limitations below.
- C1 sequential requests. Eight fresh serving processes in **ABBA / BAAB** order form four adjacent baseline/optimized restart pairs. Each process scans all eleven lengths, with three excluded warmups and eight measured requests per length. This is 32 measured requests per arm per length, not 32 independent restarts.
- Same exact-token prompts, seeds, and order in both arms; temperature 0, top-p 1, top-k 1, fixed **256 output tokens**, `ignore_eos=true`. 1M means **1,000,000 input tokens**, leaving room for generation within the server limit. Other K labels are powers of 1,024.
- GPU utilization, memory, clocks, temperature, and power are recorded at 1 Hz. Startup/JIT warmup and separate diagnostic instrumentation are excluded from measured samples. No outlier samples are silently removed.
- TTFT/TPOT use the server's per-request timestamps. **TTFT starts at scheduling**, excluding upload and queue time. **TPOT = (last output timestamp − first output timestamp) / 255**. Client-side latency is retained as a transport cross-check; SSE chunk arrival intervals are not substituted for decode time.
- Latencies below are geometric means of the four per-restart request medians. Throughput is total input + output tokens divided by the observed C1 batch interval (including client/request overhead), geometrically averaged across restarts. It is not saturated multi-client serving throughput. At a fixed input/output length, output-token throughput has the same percentage change.
- Positive improvement means **lower latency** (`1 − optimized/baseline`) or **higher throughput** (`optimized/baseline − 1`). Confidence intervals resample the four **restart pairs**, not individual requests (20,000 bootstrap draws). Four pairs give limited statistical resolution; an interval crossing zero is not proof of equivalence.

### Performance

| Context | B TTFT ms | O TTFT ms | TTFT improvement | B TPOT ms | O TPOT ms | TPOT improvement | B total tok/s | O total tok/s | Throughput improvement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1K | 152.69 | 152.04 | +0.43% | 6.323 | 6.324 | -0.02% | 723.96 | 723.82 | -0.02% |
| 2K | 151.39 | 155.69 | -2.84% | 6.468 | 6.469 | -0.02% | 1277.30 | 1273.71 | -0.28% |
| 4K | 167.71 | 168.73 | -0.60% | 6.475 | 6.476 | -0.02% | 2387.95 | 2385.88 | -0.09% |
| 8K | 298.48 | 298.25 | +0.08% | 6.478 | 6.479 | -0.01% | 4322.71 | 4322.41 | -0.01% |
| 16K | 575.13 | 575.20 | -0.01% | 6.498 | 6.499 | -0.02% | 7436.45 | 7435.08 | -0.02% |
| 32K | 1150.58 | 1150.46 | +0.01% | 6.428 | 6.429 | -0.01% | 11799.75 | 11800.18 | +0.00% |
| 64K | 2315.76 | 2280.78 | +1.51% | 6.452 | 6.452 | -0.00% | 16549.38 | 16693.37 | +0.87% |
| 128K | 4781.71 | 4605.30 | +3.69% | 6.557 | 6.557 | +0.01% | 20269.73 | 20835.80 | +2.79% |
| 256K | 10154.19 | 9371.82 | +7.70% | 6.571 | 6.573 | -0.03% | 22090.93 | 23651.89 | +7.07% |
| 512K | 22759.85 | 19417.85 | +14.68% | 6.603 | 6.604 | -0.01% | 21379.03 | 24752.65 | +15.78% |
| 1M (1,000,000) | 54154.13 | 40387.57 | +25.42% | 6.631 | 6.633 | -0.02% | 17856.28 | 23675.18 | +32.59% |

At 1M, measured TTFT improves by +25.42% and C1 total-token throughput by +32.59%. Across all lengths, TPOT improvement point estimates range from -0.03% to +0.01%. The fallback 1K–32K TTFT changes range from -2.84% to +0.43%. The intervals below and individual restart results, not just the sign of a small point estimate, determine how confidently an improvement or regression can be distinguished from run-to-run variation. These results do not prove zero overhead outside the tested configuration. Every TPOT interval includes zero: this scan does not establish a systematic TPOT change, nor does it prove exact equivalence.

**Short-input caveat:** the most negative fallback TTFT point is 2K: 151.39 → 155.69 ms (-2.84% improvement; paired 95% interval [-8.18, +2.24]%). This observation is retained, not discarded or declared harmless solely because the new collective is gated off. The scan does not establish blanket short-input non-regression or a causal explanation for this timing difference.

## Correctness / targeted accuracy A/B

This is a targeted long-context retrieval and numerical-equivalence evaluation, **not a general model-quality benchmark**. Three distinct generated record probes per length place the answer at 10%, 50%, and 90% of the prompt. Each is repeated in the four independent processes per arm: 12 observations per arm per length, but only three distinct tasks. The prompt has a non-thinking assistant boundary; greedy decoding stops normally with at most 64 output tokens.

The table reports strict expected-answer accuracy, whether the expected answer is present, and exact generated-token equality for matched prompts. Answer containment alone is a weaker check: a response can contain the correct code yet fail strict answer-only formatting by adding an explanatory sentence. Baseline A/A compares adjacent independent baseline restarts, providing a control for process-to-process repeatability. HTTP success and valid token counts alone are not treated as accuracy.

| Context | Baseline strict answer | Optimized strict answer | B answer present | O answer present | A/B exact tokens | Baseline A/A exact tokens |

| 1K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 2K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |
| 4K | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 9/9 |

Matched A/B output-token sequences agree in **130/132** comparisons; baseline A/A agrees in **98/99**. The expected answer is present in 132/132 baseline and 132/132 optimized responses. Strict answer-only format passes 127/132 baseline and 129/132 optimized responses. Answer containment does not excuse extra or conflicting text; strict answer-only formatting and full token equality are reported separately. Repeated observations of the same three tasks are not independent evidence of broad model accuracy. Multimodal inputs, MTP, other DSA models, and general reasoning quality have not been evaluated by this scan.

Inspection of both A/B mismatches (the 90%-depth task at 512K and 1M) shows the same correct access code in both responses: baseline adds an explanatory sentence, while optimized returns only the code. The baseline A/A mismatch at 1M has the same formatting distinction; optimized's own restarts also differ in formatting at 512K. No different retrieved code was observed in these probes. This is an inspection of the observed mismatches, not a claim that all possible numerical differences are formatting-only.

Additional checks:

- **54 focused PR tests pass:** row-cost balancing, gate predicates, metadata construction, and gather/reassembly coverage including 128K–1M. These tests include mocked collective/metadata checks; they are not a substitute for the distributed serving run.
- A separate instrumented TP4 pilot confirmed actual 64K/128K sharded execution and the `[65,536, 2,051]` gathered result. Its timings are excluded from the performance table.
- Real H200 DeepGEMM + CUDA top-k checks at nine lengths from 4K to 1M compare a 512-query-row batch against uneven row slices. Valid logits are exactly equal and selected top-k **sets** match. The top-k kernel's output ordering is not deterministic: different orders also occur in the baseline A/A control with identical sets. These checks do not establish bitwise equivalence of all attention outputs.
- Real Triton pool expansion plus incomplete-tail append agrees exactly with its direct reference at those nine lengths. Measurement-harness tests validate empty-text token accounting, bundled SSE responses, restart-level aggregation, and rejection of unmatched prompts or inconsistent token counts, fingerprints, and timing denominators.

**Runtime qualification / limitations:** all 704 measured performance requests complete with exactly 256 output tokens; all 264 separate retrieval requests complete. This is not an error-free-runtime claim: the common FA3 runtime emits TMA-descriptor diagnostics, which are preserved in the server logs. Two separate baseline failures were investigated before fixing the common benchmark configuration: (1) the automatically selected FlashInfer SM90 sparse MLA backend fails during 65,536-row startup/autotune; a standalone NoPE MLA probe also fails at 65,536 rows while passing 64 rows; (2) with FA3, the V2 runner fails at 256K in its slot-mapping kernel, reproduced with eager execution and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1. The legacy-runner/FA3 diagnostic then passes 256K, 512K, and 1M. Failed and synchronous diagnostic admissions are excluded from the performance table. No unrelated baseline source fix is overlaid. The common user environment also registers an unrelated SGLang operator at Python startup; neither pinned vLLM source tree has a callsite for that operator. **These results qualify only the explicit legacy-runner/FA3 configuration, not default V2 or auto-selected FlashInfer SM90 MLA.**

<details>
<summary>Exact-token client and synthetic retrieval prompt generator (save as pr54951_measure.py)</summary>

Only the local model-location setting is made portable here. The tokenizer, prompt construction, seeds, token accounting, and measurement logic are the same as the measured campaign.

```python
"""Exact-token serving measurements; raw samples are never silently discarded."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import asyncio
import hashlib
import json
import statistics
import time
from pathlib import Path

import aiohttp
import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
MODEL = Path(os.environ['MODEL_DIR'])
CONTEXTS = [1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536,
            131072, 262144, 524288, 1000000]


def prompt_tokens(tokenizer, length: int, case: int, kind: str):
    """Construct exact lengths, preserving chat boundary and a complete needle.

    The synthetic retrieval probe is a smoke test, not a general quality eval.
    Needle positions rotate through 10%, 50%, and 90% of the input.
    Performance prompts use the same public, generated record workload.
    """
    seed = 54951 + case
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    key = f'record-{case:05d}-verification'
    answer = '-'.join(rng.choice(['amber', 'cedar', 'falcon', 'ivory',
                                  'maple', 'orbit', 'pearl', 'violet'], 4))
    prefix = tokenizer.encode(
        '[gMASK]<sop><|system|>You retrieve exact information from records. '
        'Answer only the requested access code, without explanation.'
        '<|user|>Read these archived records.\n', add_special_tokens=False)
    suffix = tokenizer.encode(
        f'\nEnd of records. What is the access code for {key}? '
        'Respond with only the access code.'
        '<|assistant|>\n<think>\n</think>\n', add_special_tokens=False)
    needle = tokenizer.encode(
        f'\nThe access code for {key} is {answer}.\n', add_special_tokens=False)
    # Generate ordinary-text background once; no special/random vocabulary IDs.
    paragraphs = []
    for i in range(512):
        number = int(rng.integers(100000, 999999))
        paragraphs.append(f'Archive entry {i}: shipment {number} was received '
                          'at the northern depot. The inspection confirmed '
                          'that the supplies were dry and accounted for.\n')
    background = tokenizer.encode(''.join(paragraphs), add_special_tokens=False)
    available = length - len(prefix) - len(suffix) - len(needle)
    assert available > 0
    background = (background * ((available // len(background)) + 1))[:available]
    depth = [0.1, 0.5, 0.9][case % 3]
    position = int(available * depth)
    tokens = prefix + background[:position] + needle + background[position:] + suffix
    assert len(tokens) == length
    digest = hashlib.sha256(np.asarray(tokens, dtype='<i4').tobytes()).hexdigest()
    return tokens, {'sha256': digest, 'case': case, 'seed': seed, 'kind': kind,
                    'needle_depth': depth, 'expected_answer': answer}


async def request(session, base_url, tokens, output_len, metadata, quality=False):
    body = {
        'model': 'zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash', 'prompt': tokens,
        'max_tokens': output_len, 'temperature': 0, 'top_p': 1, 'top_k': 1,
        'seed': 54951, 'ignore_eos': not quality, 'stream': True,
        'stream_options': {'include_usage': True},
        # Streaming logprobs identify empty-text tokens without echoing a
        # million prompt IDs in the first response chunk.
        'logprobs': 5 if quality else 0, 'return_tokens_as_token_ids': True,
        'skip_special_tokens': False,
    }
    # Serialize outside the timed interval. HTTP upload remains in client TTFT.
    payload = json.dumps(body, separators=(',', ':')).encode()
    record = {**metadata, 'input_tokens': len(tokens), 'requested_output': output_len,
              'started_unix': time.time(), 'chunks': [], 'output_token_ids': [],
              'text': '', 'logprobs': [], 'server_metrics': None}
    started = time.perf_counter()
    async with session.post(base_url + '/v1/completions', data=payload,
                            headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'}) as response:
        if response.status != 200:
            raise RuntimeError(f'HTTP {response.status}: {(await response.text())[:2000]}')
        async for raw_line in response.content:
            received = time.perf_counter() - started
            line = raw_line.decode().strip()
            if not line.startswith('data: '):
                continue
            if line == 'data: [DONE]':
                break
            event = json.loads(line[6:])
            if 'error' in event:
                raise RuntimeError(event['error'])
            if event.get('metrics'):
                record['server_metrics'] = event['metrics']
            if event.get('usage'):
                record['usage'] = event['usage']
            for choice in event.get('choices', []):
                logprobs = choice.get('logprobs') or {}
                ids = [int(t.removeprefix('token_id:'))
                       for t in logprobs.get('tokens', [])]
                if ids:
                    record['chunks'].append({'t_s': received, 'n': len(ids)})
                    record['output_token_ids'].extend(ids)
                    record['logprobs'].extend(logprobs.get('token_logprobs', []))
                record['text'] += choice.get('text', '')
                if choice.get('finish_reason'):
                    record['finish_reason'] = choice['finish_reason']
    record['client_elapsed_s'] = time.perf_counter() - started
    chunks = record['chunks']
    count = len(record['output_token_ids'])
    assert chunks and count > 0, 'No identifiable output tokens received'
    assert record.get('usage', {}).get('prompt_tokens') == len(tokens), record.get('usage')
    assert record['usage']['completion_tokens'] == count, record['usage']
    if not quality:
        assert count == output_len, (count, output_len)
    record['client_ttft_ms'] = chunks[0]['t_s'] * 1000
    record['client_tpot_ms'] = ((chunks[-1]['t_s'] - chunks[0]['t_s']) * 1000 /
                              (count - 1)) if count > 1 else None
    record['output_tokens'] = count
    record['token_sha256'] = hashlib.sha256(
        np.asarray(record['output_token_ids'], dtype='<i4').tobytes()).hexdigest()
    record['retrieval_contains_answer'] = metadata['expected_answer'] in record['text']
    # The forced non-thinking boundary makes this strict answer test meaningful.
    normalized = record['text'].replace('<|endoftext|>', '').replace('<|user|>', '').strip()
    record['retrieval_exact'] = normalized == metadata['expected_answer']
    return record


async def run(args):
    output = Path(args.output)
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = output / f'{args.tag}.jsonl'
    if path.exists():
        raise FileExistsError(f'Refusing to overwrite {path}')
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(MODEL), trust_remote_code=False)
    timeout = aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=1800, connect=10)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout, trust_env=False,
                                    read_bufsize=32 * 1024 * 1024) as session:
        async with session.get(args.base_url + '/health') as response:
            assert response.status == 200
        with path.open('x') as stream:
            for length in args.contexts:
                jobs = [('warmup', i) for i in range(args.warmups)]
                jobs += [('measured', i) for i in range(args.requests)]
                prepared = {}
                for phase, i in jobs:
                    case = 1000 + i if phase == 'warmup' else i
                    prepared[phase, i] = prompt_tokens(tokenizer, length, case, args.kind)
                batch_start = None
                batch_input = batch_output = 0
                for phase, i in jobs:
                    # Same measured prompts and order in every fresh process.
                    tokens, metadata = prepared[phase, i]
                    metadata.update(arm=args.arm, tag=args.tag, phase=phase,
                                    context=length, repetition=i)
                    if phase == 'measured' and batch_start is None:
                        batch_start = time.perf_counter()
                    record = await request(session, args.base_url, tokens,
                                           args.output_len, metadata,
                                           quality=args.kind == 'correctness')
                    if phase == 'measured':
                        batch_input += len(tokens)
                        batch_output += record['output_tokens']
                        batch_end = time.perf_counter()
                    stream.write(json.dumps(record, separators=(',', ':')) + '\n')
                    stream.flush()
                    metrics = record['server_metrics'] or {}
                    print(json.dumps({'tag': args.tag, 'context': length, 'phase': phase,
                                      'i': i, 'client_ttft': record['client_ttft_ms'],
                                      'server': metrics, 'tokens': record['output_tokens'],
                                      'answer': record['retrieval_contains_answer']}), flush=True)
                if batch_start is not None:
                    summary = {'record_type': 'batch_summary', 'context': length,
                               'arm': args.arm, 'tag': args.tag, 'kind': args.kind,
                               'duration_s': batch_end - batch_start,
                               'input_tokens': batch_input, 'output_tokens': batch_output,
                               'total_tok_s': (batch_input + batch_output) / (batch_end - batch_start),
                               'output_tok_s': batch_output / (batch_end - batch_start)}
                    stream.write(json.dumps(summary) + '\n')
                    stream.flush()


if __name__ == '__main__':
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--arm', choices=['baseline', 'optimized'], required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--tag', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--output', default=str(ROOT / 'results/pr54951-current-20260907'))
    parser.add_argument('--base-url', default='http://127.0.0.1:8010')
    parser.add_argument('--contexts', nargs='+', type=int, default=CONTEXTS)
    parser.add_argument('--warmups', type=int, default=3)
    parser.add_argument('--requests', type=int, default=8)
    parser.add_argument('--output-len', type=int, default=256)
    parser.add_argument('--kind', choices=['performance', 'correctness'], default='performance')
    asyncio.run(run(parser.parse_args()))
```

</details>

AI assistance was used for implementation and benchmark analysis. The author owns validation, review follow-up, and maintenance. This PR optimizes the already-merged GLM/DSA prefill path; it is not a duplicate model-support submission.

title: [Bugfix] Stop leaking the internal field name in the max_tokens validation error
body:
## Purpose

`TokenizeParams.__post_init__` builds the "output tokens exceed the context length" message with the
f-string self-documenting specifier:

```python
f"{self.max_total_tokens_param}={max_total_tokens=}. "
```

`{max_total_tokens=}` expands to `max_total_tokens=<value>` on its own, so the public override name
is emitted and then immediately followed by the *internal attribute name*. A deployment that remaps
the name — which the field exists to allow ("Override this to edit the message for validation
errors") — produces:

```
max_tokens=20000 cannot be greater than max_model_len=max_total_tokens=8192.
```

`max_total_tokens` is an internal field: it is not a request body field and not a server flag
(`--max-model-len` is the user-facing one). So the 400 error tells the client about a name it cannot
set, and the doubled `name=name=` looks like a formatting bug even when the remapping is the default.

Reproduced directly: constructing `TokenizeParams(max_total_tokens=8192, max_output_tokens=20000)`
before the fix yields `... cannot be greater than max_total_tokens=max_total_tokens=8192.`

## Fix

Drop the trailing `=` so the value is interpolated plainly. This matches the sibling truncation
message a few lines below (`vllm/renderers/params.py:250`), which already writes
`{max_input_tokens}` without the specifier — so the corrected form is the one the file uses
elsewhere, not a new convention.

## Test plan

Added `tests/renderers/test_params_validation.py`:

- `test_max_output_error_uses_public_name_once` — remaps both parameter names, asserts the message
  reads `max_tokens=20000 cannot be greater than max_model_len=8192` and that the string
  `max_total_tokens` does **not** appear anywhere in it.
- `test_max_output_error_with_default_names` — pins the default-name rendering so the fix cannot
  simply delete the value.

Verified locally on an editable install of `main`:

| check | result |
|---|---|
| with the fix | 2 passed |
| fix reverted | the first test **fails** |
| `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `typos`, `check-spdx-header`, `check-test-tethering` | all pass |

Only the message text changes; no signature, no control flow, no behavior a client can depend on
other than the error string itself.

title: [CI] Shard (H100) Helion Kernels five ways
body:
## What
Raise `(H100) Helion Kernels Shard %N` from 2 to 5 hash shards of the whole `kernels/helion/` directory, so each shard stays under the 20-minute target. The MI250 mirror is pinned at its current 2 replicas so the new base count does not multiply it.

## Old
```
kernels-helion-test       parallelism: 2   pytest kernels/helion/ --shard-id/--num-shards
  mirror amd (MI250)      inherits 2
```

## New
```
kernels-helion-test       parallelism: 5   pytest kernels/helion/ --shard-id/--num-shards   (command unchanged)
  mirror amd (MI250)      parallelism: 2   (explicit; unchanged behaviour)
```

## Notes
- No coverage change: same command on the same directory, and no filters before or after. Only the replica count changes.
- The directory has ~1,970 run cases per build. Each of 5 shards gets ~390, so no shard is empty.
- A named semantic split was considered and rejected. `test_rms_norm_per_block_quant.py` is about half of the job's pytest time on its own, so it would need a monolith split before it could fit in one job.
- Legacy `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` is untouched.

## Expected runtime and overhead
Predictions based on recent `main` builds (e.g. [91049](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91049), [91027](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/91027)):

| Job / replica | pytest | running wall | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before: shard 1–2 (each) | ~34–40m | ~40–46m | ~1–10m | `pip install helion`, image pull when cold |
| after: shard 1–5 (each, predicted) | ~14–16m | ~15–17m | ~1m warm | same, now paid 5× |

- Baseline → new: ~81 → ~86 worker-minutes (predicted). That is about **+5 extra worker-minutes**, within the 20-minute budget, and comes from three extra setups.
- Slowest shard: ~16m pytest (predicted), inside the 20m target.
- Why 5: 4 shards would put each at ~19.6m of pytest with no headroom for hash skew or run-to-run variation.

title: [Perf][MoE] Tile pack_bitmatrix by 32 rows instead of 512
body:
## Purpose

`make_routing_data` launches `pack_bitmatrix` with `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 512`. The kernel masks its row tail on both the load and the store, so the packed bitmatrix is bit-identical for any tile width; the tile width is purely a launch-config choice. It is a bad one: the cost of each program is dominated by the `[BLOCK_SIZE_M, BLOCK_SIZE_K]` one-hot `tl.where` / `tl.reduce_or`, which Triton emits at full tile width whether or not those rows exist. A 512-row tile therefore pays for padding rows at every batch size, and for any batch of up to 512 tokens (every decode step at realistic concurrency) it collapses the grid to a single workgroup. This PR changes the tile to 32 rows, matching `BLOCK_SIZE_K`.

**Who reaches this.** `make_routing_data` runs once per MoE layer per step wherever the OAI Triton experts rebuild routing from top-k ids on triton_kernels 3.5.1/3.6:

- **DeepSeek-V4 on MI300X/MI325X (gfx942), with the recommended `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`.** `AiterExperts` rejects MXFP4 weights off gfx950, so DeepSeek-V4's ROCm candidate list (`[AITER_MXFP4_BF16, TRITON_UNFUSED]`) falls through to `TRITON_UNFUSED`, and `UnfusedOAITritonExperts` calls `make_routing_data` unconditionally. With AITER off, gfx942 cannot run DeepSeek-V4 at all (the sparse-attention indexer requires AITER there), so this is the only configuration.
- gpt-oss on the OAI Triton path under expert parallelism (TP=1 bypasses it since #45457), and anything that explicitly selects `--moe-backend triton` / `triton_unfused`.

**Not affected:** gfx950 with AITER on (DeepSeek-V4 and gpt-oss both select AITER MoE backends there); triton_kernels 3.8 (the `Dockerfile.rock` image), whose `make_routing_data` builds routing in torch and never launches `pack_bitmatrix`; and eager mode / prefill, where the call is host-bound.

**Related:** #43159 rewrites `pack_bitmatrix` itself and adds a runtime-compiled (`load_inline`) HIP fast path. It leaves `BLOCK_SIZE_M = 512` in `make_routing_data`, and its Triton fallback still defaults to 512, so the two compose: this PR is the one-constant change on its own and is useful whether or not #43159 lands.

## Test Plan

MI325X (gfx942), TP=1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, main `6697a7dd30` built from source for gfx942. The branch is rebased onto `f34a0e0797`; none of the intervening commits touch the changed files.

- Unit test: the new `test_pack_bitmatrix_independent_of_block_size_m` packs the same top-k ids at tile widths 8…1024 and asserts bit-identical output against 512, on row counts that are not tile multiples, with and without `-1` (non-local expert) slots, plus sentinel guard rows that catch writes past `n_rows`.
- Reach: in-process counters on `make_routing_data` / `pack_bitmatrix`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash truncated to 6 layers with dummy weights; gpt-oss-120b as the negative control.
- Micro: the whole `make_routing_data` call under CUDA-graph replay and eager, 5 routing shapes × 8 row counts, blocks of 4 runs per arm (main, PR, main again) with the first discarded.
- e2e: a fresh server per run, main ×4 then PR ×4 on one card with the first run of each block discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 4096 \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --moe-backend triton_unfused \
    --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 300 --max-concurrency 37 --seed 1234
```

- Accuracy: lm_eval `gsm8k`, 5-shot, greedy, all 1319 items, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`, same serving config as e2e. The main arm was run twice.
- gfx950 (MI355X) no-regression: the same micro on a triton_kernels 3.6 install (main `c961121519` Python on the v0.30.0 ROCm image's binaries), reach counters with AITER on, and the same e2e with AITER off on a triton_kernels 3.8 image (main `8b84e15066` Python on that image's binaries). Per-run detail in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58546#issuecomment-5825325064).

## Test Result

**Unit test:** main 48/48, PR 48/48. A copy of the PR tree with the store mask removed fails 40/48.

**Reach:**

| model | MoE backend | `make_routing_data` calls |
|---|---|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, AITER on | `TRITON_UNFUSED` | 114 (6 layers × 19 steps) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, AITER off | engine refuses to start on gfx942 | — |
| gpt-oss-120b, AITER on (control) | `AITER_TRITON_MXFP4_BF16` | 0 |

**Micro**, CUDA-graph replay, DeepSeek-V4-Flash routing (256 experts, top-6, TP=1), µs per call (median of 3 runs; all ranges disjoint, main-vs-main drift median 0.72 %):

| rows | main | PR | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 70.00 | 35.60 | +49.2 % |
| 50 | 76.43 | 40.41 | +47.1 % |
| 333 | 85.70 | 49.79 | +41.9 % |
| 4099 | 82.94 | 46.96 | +43.4 % |
| 16384 | 91.63 | 56.02 | +38.9 % |

Across all 40 configs (gpt-oss TP=1 / EP=2, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP=1 / EP=2, DeepSeek-V4-Pro EP=8) the median gain is +29.1 % (+16.8 % to +49.8 %). The saving is roughly constant in row count, about 36 µs per call here. Eager is flat (−0.8 %, inside the 3.1 % main-vs-main drift) because the call is host-bound there.

**e2e**, in 1024 / out 512, 300 prompts, concurrency 37 (3 / 3 warm runs; throughput ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 1390.3 | 1407.4 | +1.2 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 2564.9 | 2528.0 | −1.4 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 3106.5 | 3107.6 | +0.0 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 71.45 | 70.54 | −1.3 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 71.79 | 70.85 | −1.3 % |

TPOT falls about 0.9 ms per step while median TTFT is unchanged, so the gain is in decode; 43 MoE layers × ~36 µs bounds it at ~1.5 ms per step. The effect is about the size of the within-arm spread.

**gfx950 (MI355X): no regression** ([per-run detail](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58546#issuecomment-5825325064)):

| configuration | changed line executes | result |
|---|---|---|
| triton_kernels 3.6, micro | yes | graph replay faster at 40/40 shapes (median +26.9 %, +16.1 % to +47.1 %); eager +0.3 %, inside the 2.1 % main-vs-main drift |
| `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` | no: `AiterExperts`, 0 `make_routing_data` calls (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, gpt-oss-120b) | unaffected |
| AITER off, triton_kernels 3.8, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP=1 e2e (4 / 4 warm runs) | no: 114 `make_routing_data` calls, 0 `pack_bitmatrix` launches | total tok/s +0.25 %, mean TPOT −0.20 %, median TTFT −0.00 %, all inside the within-arm range |

No gfx950 e2e here executes the changed line: triton 3.8 cannot run the 3.6 `matmul_ogs` on gfx950 (`OutOfResources` in the MoE GEMM, independent of this change), so that needs the triton 3.7 + triton_kernels 3.6 pairing `Dockerfile.rocm` ships.

**GSM8K** (strict-match):

| model | main | main (repeat) | PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | 0.9553 | 0.9553 | 0.9553 |

1318/1319 generations are identical between main and PR, and every item gets the same verdict.

title: [ROCm] Harden DeepSeek-V4 sparse prefill against zero-query-token chunks
body:
`_forward_prefill()` can be handed a prefill chunk covering zero query tokens,
and `combine_topk_swa_indices()` cannot reshape that. This adds the missing
guard.

## How an empty chunk arises

`_forward_prefill()` chunks the prefill range by request count with
`PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4`, over the range reported by
`split_decodes_and_prefills()`, which returns `num_prefills` as a suffix,
`num_reqs - first_prefill`. Request slots with zero query tokens are never
themselves flagged as prefills, but any that trail the first real prefill fall
inside that suffix. Such slots are an intentional artifact of request-dimension
padding: `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/input_batch.py` writes
`query_start_loc[num_reqs + 1:] = num_tokens`, and
`split_decodes_and_prefills()` documents them itself ("some requests may have a
query length of 0 but since they are padding ...").

Once `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE` such slots trail the last real prefill, a whole chunk
covers zero query tokens and `topk_indices.reshape(topk_indices.shape[0], -1)`
becomes ambiguous.

## Change

Hoist the query range computation above the K-cache gathers (it only reads
`query_start_loc_cpu`) and skip chunks with an empty range. This also drops two
`dequantize_and_gather_k_cache()` calls and one `rocm_sparse_attn_prefill()`
launch per padding-only chunk, which had nothing to compute.

## What I can show

Driving the real `split_decodes_and_prefills()` and replaying the real chunk
loop over `[1 + k, 256] + [0] * pad`, for `k` (`num_speculative_tokens`) in
`{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7}` and `pad` in `{0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 8}`:

| | unguarded | guarded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| shapes that raise | 21 / 42 | 0 / 42 |
| non-empty chunks executed | identical, 0 mismatches | |

The 21 are exactly those with `pad >= PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE`. `k` does not enter
the condition, so this is not specific to speculative decoding. Copy-paste
reproduction, no GPU or weights needed:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55695#issuecomment-5580073174

## What I cannot show

Reachability on `main`. The state was hit for real on v0.26.0 (full traceback,
all four TP ranks, `EngineDeadError`), but on current `main` two full DSpark
runs with the same configuration produced zero empty chunks across 90,988
instrumented prefill-chunk invocations:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55695#issuecomment-5578723131

So this is hardening a path that is reachable by construction, not a fix for an
observable regression. Reasonable to decline on that basis — I would still
argue for it since the suffix semantics and the padding convention are both
unchanged, and the guard removes work rather than adding it.

---

Reviewed and verified by Zheng Gong <zgong@amd.com>.

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Use the shared prefill chunk plan in the ROCm sparse prefill
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekV41ROCMAiterMLAAttention._forward_prefill` splits prefill requests into fixed groups of `PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE = 4` and sizes the bf16 gather workspace from the static worst case (`N = ceil(max_model_len / compress_ratio)`, `M = N + window_size + max_num_batched_tokens`). The NVIDIA V4.1 paths already use `DeepseekSparseSWAMetadata.get_prefill_chunk_plan()`, which packs requests by workspace area and returns each chunk's real widths.

This PR drives the ROCm V4.1 prefill loop from the same plan. As on NVIDIA, it passes `has_compressed=not swa_only`, because ratio-1 layers carry a compressed region. Each chunk's KV is a `(chunk_size, chunk_M, head_dim)` view of the single prefill workspace, which also holds the MXFP8 staging rows, and `chunk_N` / `chunk_M` go to the SWA gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices`.

The ROCm V4.1 combine runs two `torch.repeat_interleave` calls per chunk, each forcing a host sync, so steps with more than 4 prefill requests gain the most. Peak memory is unchanged: the plan's area bound equals the worst case that `forward_mqa()` already reserves during warmup. Decode is unchanged, and steps with at most 4 prefills still run as a single chunk.

The same change for DeepSeek-V4 is #58405. #56720 touches this loop and composes with it.

## Test Plan

MI355X (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, `kv_cache_dtype=fp8`, main `bbd7c24d6e`.

- **Micro:** time `_forward_prefill` on live model inputs for main vs. this PR, in interleaved blocks within one process. Each scenario is one prefill step. The model is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash truncated to 6 layers with dummy weights (compress ratios 0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1), TP=1, `max_model_len=65536`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`.
- **Reach:** under the default serving config, where main selects `CompilationMode.NONE` with FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs for V4.1, `_forward_prefill` runs on every prefill step on all layers.
- **e2e:** real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP=2, a fresh server per run, 4 runs per arm per block with the first discarded, one server on the host at a time.

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 307 --random-output-len 23 --random-range-ratio 0.25 \
    --num-prompts 1021 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- **e2e at TP=4, 1k/1k:** one server per arm (warmed, prefix caching off), `--max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-num-seqs 512`, `--num-prompts` = 10 × concurrency, 3 runs per point.

```bash
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio <0|0.25> \
    --num-prompts <10 x conc> --max-concurrency <512|128|32> --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1234
```

- **Accuracy:** `lm_eval --model vllm --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto`, greedy, `max_model_len=4096`, `seed=1234`, on real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=2. Main was run three times and this PR twice.

## Test Result

**Micro:** sum over 6 layers, median of 3 runs, noise floor ≤ 0.9 %.

| prefill step | chunks main → PR | main (ms) | PR (ms) | speedup |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 × 11777 tokens | 1 → 1 | 18.5 | 18.5 | −0.0 % |
| 7 × 400–1800 | 2 → 1 | 16.6 | 11.6 | +43 % |
| 13 × 700–1100 | 4 → 1 | 29.8 | 15.0 | +99 % |
| 29 × 170–430 | 8 → 1 | 45.3 | 11.2 | +305 % |
| 53 × 90–250 | 14 → 1 | 74.6 | 10.3 | +621 % |

On gfx950, part of the gain comes from larger chunks crossing the 1024-query threshold that sends them to AITER OPUS (#54855). With routing pinned to Triton, the gains are +24 / +51 / +189 / +411 %, and outputs are bit-identical.

**e2e**, 1021 prompts in 307 / out 23 (6 warm runs per arm, ranges disjoint):

| metric | main | PR | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total tok/s | 14563 | 22407 | +53.9 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 11678 | 7359 | −37.0 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 11677 | 7282 | −37.6 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 502.4 | 327.9 | −34.8 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 499.0 | 329.0 | −34.1 % |

With `--max-concurrency 3`, no step carries more than 3 prefills, so every step runs as one chunk on both sides (Δ of medians, PR vs main):

| workload | warm runs | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| in 1033 / out 131, 61 prompts, concurrency 3 | 6 / 6 | −0.9 % | +2.0 % | +2.4 % | +0.8 % | +0.7 % |

The two arms' ranges overlap (p = 0.07), and within-block drift is ±1 %.

**e2e at TP=4, 1k/1k** (median of 3 runs, Δ PR vs main):

| range ratio | concurrency | Total tok/s | Mean TTFT | Median TTFT | Mean TPOT | Median TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 512 | +6.9 % | −19.4 % | −19.9 % | −4.7 % | −4.5 % |
| 0 | 128 | +3.4 % | −16.9 % | −43.0 % | −1.6 % | +2.5 % |
| 0 | 32 | +2.6 % | −22.4 % | −24.0 % | −0.6 % | −0.1 % |
| 0.25 | 512 | +0.0 % | −15.8 % | +0.7 % | +0.3 % | +0.3 % |
| 0.25 | 128 | +0.5 % | −12.0 % | −0.3 % | −0.3 % | −0.2 % |
| 0.25 | 32 | −0.1 % | −6.9 % | +0.7 % | +0.2 % | +0.3 % |

With fixed lengths (ratio 0), finished requests are replaced together, so every wave of admissions is a prefill step with dozens of requests. Throughput ranges are disjoint at each concurrency, and the gain is mostly in TTFT.

With ratio 0.25, completions spread out and later steps rarely carry more than 4 prefills. Throughput and median latency are unchanged; only the opening burst gets faster, which shows up in mean TTFT.

**GSM8K** (strict-match):

| model | main | main (repeats) | PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 0.9318 | 0.9310 / 0.9310 | 0.9272 / 0.9295 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (does not reach this path) | 0.7013 | 0.7081 | 0.7028 / 0.7089 |

The standard error is ±0.007 for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Its per-sample agreement between main and the PR falls within the range between main's own runs.
