title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Restore the fused query RMSNorm + MXFP8 quantization path
body:
## Purpose

`can_fuse_query_quant` decides whether the DeepSeek-V4.1 attention block may hand `wq_b` a pre-quantized query, letting `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` do the q/kv RMSNorm and the MXFP8 quantization in one kernel. It probed `linear.input_quant_key`. #53793 renamed that attribute to the private `_input_quant_key` and introduced `get_input_quant_key` as its reader, but this call site was not updated, and it is the last one in the tree still reading the old name. The gate has been unconditionally `False` since that rename, so every layer runs a BF16 `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` followed by a standalone `MXFP8QuantizeSwizzled` over the query — exactly the pair the fused kernel exists to replace.

Read the capability through `get_input_quant_key`, and pass `launch_pdl` to the fused kernel's launch. The kernel already compiles in `gdc_wait()` / `gdc_launch_dependents()` from its `LAUNCH_PDL` constexpr, but without the launch attribute Triton issues an ordinary launch, so the kernel cannot start before its predecessor retires and the wait is inert. Its siblings `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant` and the Qwen4 PLE/HC kernels pass both. The fused path is CUDA-only by construction, since `can_fuse_query_quant` returns `False` off CUDA, so the new kwarg is never reached on ROCm.

This restores a lost fusion; it does not change model output. The fused kernel reproduces the separate-kernel FP8 bytes, swizzled scales and normalized KV bit for bit.

## Duplicate-work check

No issue tracks this, so issue-number checks are not applicable. Open-PR searches covered `can_fuse_query_quant`, `input_quant_key`, `get_input_quant_key`, `query_quant deepseek_v41`, `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm`, `launch_pdl triton` and `deepseek_v41 pdl`. Nothing else touches `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py`. #53793 performed the rename that stranded this gate. #55505 extends the same contract with input scales and does not change how the key is read. #48086 also adds a missing `launch_pdl`, but in `deepseek_v4/common/ops/fused_inv_rope_fp8_quant.py`, for a `TypeError` on non-PDL hardware rather than a lost overlap. #54063 and #53151 teach ROCm AITER kernels to consume `QuantizedActivation` instead of fixing a producer gate.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH=/usr/local/cuda-13.1/bin:$PATH .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/ops/query_quant.py
```

The existing suite already encodes this gate: `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` asserts `can_fuse_query_quant` is true for the two FlashInfer MXFP8 kernels and that the pre-quantized `wq_b` projection matches the BF16 path at `rtol=0, atol=0`. It needs Blackwell plus a FlashInfer that can JIT, so `nvcc` must be on `PATH` or the whole group skips, which is how the regression went unnoticed.

Two standalone harnesses, not included in the diff, produced the numbers below. One times the isolated production chain `fused_wqa_wkv` GEMM → q/kv RMSNorm (+ query quantization) → `wq_b` GEMM and compares outputs bitwise before timing. The other serves the model and sweeps client concurrency, running both code versions inside one job so they share a node, with the order counterbalanced across two jobs.

## Test Result

Standalone commit `20538d465a`, based on `9d75dd4544`. **73 tests passed** in 107 s on GB200. On `main` the same file reports **24 failed**, all of them `test_shared_query_quant_preserves_projection` cases failing at `assert can_fuse_query_quant([linear, linear])`, so no new test was needed. Changed-file pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, ruff format, typos and mypy 3.10.

Model output is unchanged. The microbenchmark checked FP8 data, swizzled scales, normalized KV and the downstream `wq_b` GEMM output for bitwise equality against the two-kernel path at all 14 shapes before timing, and the projection test asserts the same at `rtol=0, atol=0`. No accuracy evaluation is claimed, because the change cannot move a logit.

### Performance
Serving: `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` with `indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4` and `indexer_sparse_logits`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-num-seqs 128`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`. Client is `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, 1024 input and 256 output tokens, `--ignore-eos` and `--temperature 0` so every request runs exactly 255 decode steps. Concurrency 1 is repeated 10 times and the others 5 times; each cell is the median of per-run medians. The two columns of raw ITL are the two jobs.

| Concurrency | Base ITL (ms) | Patched ITL (ms) | ITL Gain |
|------------:|--------------:|-----------------:|---------:|
| 1   | 5.020 / 5.055   | 4.983 / 5.037   | 0.55% |
| 8   | 6.321 / 6.357   | 6.255 / 6.295   | 1.01% |
| 32  | 8.313 / 8.325   | 8.309 / 8.142   | 1.12% |
| 256 | 12.153 / 12.157 | 12.076 / 12.127 | 0.44% |

All eight paired measurements favour the patched build and swapping the order flips no sign. Concurrency 8 is the most trustworthy row: the two jobs agree at 1.05% and 0.97%, and 48 tokens per step is the shape where the microbenchmark predicts 69.7 us out of a 6.32 ms step, or 1.10%. 


## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted with the investigation, the benchmarks and this description. Juntian Liu requested this PR after reviewing the root cause, the measured gains and the benchmark caveats.

title: [Kernel] Avoid redundant SM100 blockwise FP8 scale padding
body:
## Purpose

The SM100 blockwise FP8 GEMM requires the leading dimension of its
column-major activation scales to be divisible by four for TMA scale-factor
copies.

The current implementation handles a non-aligned `M > 64` by allocating a
temporary padded scale tensor and issuing a `cudaMemcpy2DAsync` before every
GEMM. This is correct and significantly faster than falling back to the
`swapAB` kernel, but the allocation and copy are unnecessary when vLLM owns
the activation quantization step.

This PR makes the vLLM CUTLASS block-FP8 path produce TMA-aligned activation
scales directly during quantization. The GEMM then derives the physical scale
extent from `a_scales.stride(1)` and consumes the aligned tensor without an
additional allocation or copy.

The change preserves compatibility with direct custom-op callers:

- TMA-aligned scales use the zero-allocation, zero-copy fast path.
- Packed, non-aligned scales retain the existing temporary-padding fallback.
- The existing `M <= 64` `swapAB` heuristic is unchanged.
- There is no public API change.

The persistent storage overhead is at most three FP32 scale entries per
`K / 128` scale column, while the per-GEMM temporary allocation is removed
from the normal vLLM path.

### Lossless behavior

This is a physical-layout optimization only. It does not change the logical
scale values, FP8 quantization, kernel math, accumulation type, or output
type.

Packed and aligned paths were compared with `torch.equal` for
`M = 13, 64, 65, 66, 67, 125, 511, 1026, 2047`:

| Comparison | Result | Maximum absolute difference |
|---|---:|---:|
| Quantized FP8 activations | Bitwise identical | 0 |
| Logical FP32 scales | Bitwise identical | 0 |
| GEMM-only BF16 output | Bitwise identical | 0 |
| Quantization + GEMM BF16 output | Bitwise identical | 0 |

The separately reported 0.11%-0.15% relative error is the expected error of
the FP8/BF16 result relative to an FP32 dequantized reference. Both the packed
baseline and aligned fast path have the same error and are bitwise identical
to each other.

## Test Plan

1. Rebuild the stable-ABI CUDA extension with the SM100 CUTLASS kernels.
2. Run focused correctness tests for both scale layouts across:
   - the `M = 64/65` dispatch boundary;
   - all non-zero `M % 4` residue classes;
   - tiny, medium, and multi-scale-atom `M` values;
   - a non-128-aligned weight dimension.
3. Compare packed and aligned quantization outputs and GEMM outputs bitwise.
4. Benchmark both paths after five warmup iterations:
   - GEMM-only: reuse the output tensor to isolate scale-padding overhead;
   - end-to-end: include activation quantization, tensor allocation, and GEMM.
5. Run the repository pre-commit hooks on all modified files.

Representative commands:

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py::test_w8a8_block_fp8_cutlass_matmul

pre-commit run --files \
  csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_blockwise_sm100_fp8_dispatch.cuh \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py
```

## Test Result

### Correctness

- Stable-ABI SM100 extension build: **PASS**
- Focused CUDA correctness cases: **9/9 PASS**
- Bitwise packed-versus-aligned comparison: **9/9 PASS**
- Pre-commit hooks, including Ruff, clang-format, mypy, and test tethering:
  **PASS**

### Performance

Measured on an NVIDIA L20D. Each value is the arithmetic mean across these
five model GEMM shapes:

- `N=5120, K=4096`
- `N=4096, K=2048`
- `N=512, K=4096`
- `N=4096, K=256`
- `N=4608, K=4096`

`Speedup = packed baseline wall time / aligned fast-path wall time`; higher is
better.

| M | GEMM-only wall-time speedup | Quantization + GEMM wall-time speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 | 1.169x | 1.149x |
| 511 | 1.171x | 1.118x |
| 2,047 | 1.128x | 1.058x |
| 8,191 | 1.065x | 1.034x |
| 63,798 | 1.027x | 1.012x |

The benefit is largest for smaller token counts, where the allocation and copy
are a significant fraction of the GEMM latency. For large compute-bound GEMMs,
the improvement converges toward 1%, while narrow `N` or `K` shapes still show
larger gains.

Selected per-shape end-to-end results:

| M | N | K | Packed wall time | Aligned wall time | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 65 | 5,120 | 4,096 | 0.0487 ms | 0.0429 ms | 1.136x |
| 65 | 4,096 | 2,048 | 0.0444 ms | 0.0382 ms | 1.161x |
| 65 | 512 | 4,096 | 0.0480 ms | 0.0416 ms | 1.155x |
| 65 | 4,096 | 256 | 0.0435 ms | 0.0375 ms | 1.160x |
| 63,798 | 5,120 | 4,096 | 1.7230 ms | 1.7096 ms | 1.008x |
| 63,798 | 512 | 4,096 | 0.6449 ms | 0.6341 ms | 1.017x |

No documentation update is required because this change does not alter the
public interface or supported model set.

title: [Bugfix] Fix Rust frontend startup with config-only model
body:
## Purpose

Fix Rust frontend startup when the model is provided through `--config`.

When running:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve --config config.yml
```

the resolved model is stored in `args.model`, while `args.model_tag` remains unset. The Rust frontend bootstrap requires `model_tag` in `--args-json`, causing startup to fail with:

```text
invalid JSON arguments: missing field `model_tag`
```

This was reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` through the vLLM Recipes flow.

## Changes

- Fall back to `args.model` when `args.model_tag` is not set.
- Explicitly pass the resolved model as `model_tag` to the Rust frontend.
- Add a regression test for config-only model selection.

This keeps positional model behavior unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py \
  -k "rust_frontend"
```

Manual validation:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve --config config.yml
```

Verify the Rust frontend `--args-json` includes:

```json
"model_tag": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B"
```

and the server starts without the `missing field model_tag` error.

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Refresh online NVFP4 scales before reload post-processing
body:
## Problem and change

Online NVFP4 reuses its MoE kernel and quantization config across weight reloads. Conversion installs new weight-scale tensors on the layer, but the reused config still references the previous alpha storage. Expert post-processing can therefore rebuild derived scales (for example TRTLLM's `g1_scale_c`) using the previous weights' scales. Restoring graph-visible parameter storage afterward is too late to correct those derived values.

Copy the converted `w13_scale_2` and `w2_scale_2` values into the persistent config alphas before expert post-processing. Preserve the kernel, config, and alpha storage identities. This follows up the kernel reuse introduced by #50074; it does not rebuild the kernel or change quantization policy.

Extend the existing lifecycle test with changed scales over three processing calls. Check the values visible during expert post-processing and stable config/alpha storage.

## Related work

Checked open reload/scale work, including #49789, #50521, #50538 and #53741. Those address broader reload arenas, CUTLASS/B12x runtime storage, or ModelOpt reload. None modifies `online/nvfp4.py` to refresh an already-reused config before expert post-processing. This is the narrow online-NVFP4 refresh; broader storage work may eventually subsume it.

## Validation

- On upstream base `606d124b377e6462fe0f9076df4d50c88e4dcf48`, the extended existing test fails before the fix: expert post-processing observes the preceding alpha values on the first changed-weight reload. It passes with this fix.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, and repository checks. The port adds explicit non-null alpha assertions for current-main typing.
- Focused test command on this CPU-only login node (using the existing dependency environment):

```bash
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" uv run --no-project --python /home/matej/prime-rl-pd-validation/.venv/bin/python python -c 'import vllm.platforms; from vllm.platforms.cpu import CpuPlatform; vllm.platforms._current_platform=CpuPlatform(); import pytest; raise SystemExit(pytest.main(["--confcutdir=tests/quantization", "tests/quantization/test_online.py::test_online_nvfp4_reuses_kernel_when_weights_are_reprocessed", "-q"]))'
```

- Earlier B300 component validation of the same seven-line fix used the GLM-5.3 RL deployment's older vLLM base (`2e6816c274496e0a6436773bfa3c1c640b64567b`) and the FlashInfer TRTLLM NVFP4 expert backend. Reloaded versus freshly loaded identical weights had approximately 9.58% and 22.49% relative output RMS error for deliberate 1.1x and 0.9x weight changes before the fix. Afterward both were bit-identical, including replay of a graph captured before reload. Same-weight reload was already exact. These deliberately large changes expose the bug; they are not estimates of normal optimizer-step error.
- No new full-model evaluation or GPU validation on current main was run for this draft. Earlier full-model GLM-5.3 RL measurements retained approximately 0.04–0.05 KL and included a separate trainer experiment, so they do not establish model-level improvement from this fix alone.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex investigated, ported the fix, extended the regression test, and prepared this draft. Submitted as a draft for collaborator assessment; human review and current-main GPU/model validation remain pending.

title: [Kimi-K3][Perf] Dispatch GEMM for vision patch embedder
body:
## Purpose

Kimi K2.5/K3 passes contiguous `[patches, 3, 14, 14]` inputs to its shared vision tower. Each Conv2d call produces one output per patch, so use the existing `Conv2dLayer.forward_native` GEMM path. Checkpoint keys and output shape stay the same; the explicit output width also handles zero patches.

**Alternative considered**:  We decide not to add GEMM dispatch to `Conv2dLayer.forward_cuda` because it serves many other models with different input layouts, which might not guarantee speedup by switching to GEMM. For example, GLM5Next forms a channels-last NCHW view with `view(..., 2, 2, C).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)` before its 2×2 feature merger. A
GB300 BF16 microbenchmark of a representative 1024→4096 merger shows GEMM regression.

title: [CI] Run DFlash2 NVFP4 acceptance test on B200; skip it on H200 35GB MIG
body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Spec Decode AL DFlash Nightly` (`spec-decode-dflash-nightly`) has failed 18 nightlies in a row. Right now the only failure is `test_dflash_correctness[qwen3.8-dflash2-nvfp4-mrv2]` (1 failed, 5 passed). Latest failure: https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90771#01a0d019-ffc5-47a3-954a-14cfa549c6e9

The config (target `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` + draft `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`) was added in #55960. It doesn't fit on a 35GB MIG slice:

- budget: 0.85 × 32.5 GiB = 27.62 GiB
- weights: 22.88 GiB (H200 has no native FP4, so this goes through the Marlin fallback)
- CUDA graphs: 1.11 GiB
- KV cache: **-0.53 GiB**, so `ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks`

This PR:
1. Deselects the dflash2 config on the H200 35GB step with `-k "not dflash2"`. #55960 already did the same for the MI300 mirror. The other 5 params (qwen3 mrv1/mrv2, laguna-nvfp4, reference ALs) still run on H200.
2. Adds `:nvidia: (B200) Spec Decode AL DFlash2 Nightly` (`spec-decode-dflash2-nightly-b200`, `b200-k8s`, optional/nightly, 60 min). It runs only `-k "dflash2"`, with the same source deps as the DFlash nightly step minus the Laguna file. B200 has enough memory for this model and native FP4.

### Why not #58250
#58250 reverts #55960 entirely, including the fused DFlash2 kernel and its test. The kernel isn't the problem. The problem is that the test was scheduled on hardware too small for the model. Note that the `6.14 * 0.95` acceptance-length threshold has never passed on any CI hardware, so the first B200 run will be the first real check of that threshold. It may still need tuning.

### Not a duplicate
I ran `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "dflash"`. The only related open PR is the #58250 revert. No open PR moves or deselects this config.

## Test Plan / Result
- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml`: passed, including the Buildkite explicit-key and test-tethering hooks.
- Parsed the YAML and confirmed step keys are unique and the commands for the two DFlash steps are as intended.
- Param id `qwen3.8-dflash2-nvfp4-mrv2` is the only id in `tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/` that contains `dflash2`. So `-k "dflash2"` and `-k "not dflash2"` split the suite exactly.
- Not run on hardware. The B200 step will be exercised by the next nightly, or it can be triggered manually.

title: [CI] Shard (H200 MIG 35GB) PyTorch Compilation + (MI300) mirror into whole coverage units
body:
## What

Splits the `(H200 MIG 35GB) PyTorch Compilation` job into four named jobs — one per heavy test file plus the original job running the rest — and gives each of the four jobs its own `(MI300)` mirror. No test selection changes: every file still runs exactly once per lane, with no `-k`/`-m`/`--ignore` anywhere, and each file keeps its own pytest process (see #28965).

| label | key | contents |

The legacy `test-amd.yaml` copy of the MI300 job (separate `amd-ci` pipeline) is untouched.

## Notes

- Coverage is verified statically: the union of the new per-lane commands is exactly the 13 files the old `find` command collected, each claimed once. New files added at `compile/` root must now be listed in exactly one job (noted in a YAML comment) — this replaces the future-proofing the `find` glob used to provide.
- The MI300 lane stays as `mirror.amd` blocks (one per split job) so it remains tracked in the dashboard alongside its NVIDIA job; an earlier revision used two standalone AMD steps.

- AI assistance was used for this change (evidence gathering, YAML edit, local render check). No duplicate PR exists: open-PR search for this job/area found only unrelated torch.compile work.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Predictions from the job's own recent CI history (three consecutive runs, per-file pytest times parsed from logs):

| job | predicted pytest | predicted running wall | main overhead cause |

| PyTorch Compilation / Dynamic Shapes | ~18 min | ~22 min | checkout + image pull + env setup |

On the primary lane that is ≈ +13 worker-minutes against the same coverage, within the 20 extra worker-minute budget (measured ≈ +1 in build 90781). title: [ROCm] Cut 69 wasted contiguous copies per decode step from the skinny GEMM path
body:
## Summary

`rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` hoists a contiguous copy above the two branches
that consume it:

```python
if use_skinny:
    x_view = x.reshape(-1, x.size(-1)).contiguous()      # always runs
    if (m == 1 or m > 8) and 0 < n <= 5:
        return wvSplitK(..., x_view, ...)                # uses it
    elif m % 4 == 0 and n == 1 and k <= 8192 and bias is None:
        return LLMM1(..., x_view, ...)                   # uses it
    # neither matched -> fall through

if rocm_aiter_ops.is_tgemm_enabled():
    return tgemm.mm(x, weight, bias)                     # uses ORIGINAL x
return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)       # uses ORIGINAL x
```

The outer `use_skinny` gate is broad — ROCm gfx9/gfx11, fp16/bf16,
`k % 8 == 0` — while the inner conditions are narrow (`0 < n <= 5`, or
`n == 1`). Any shape that passes the gate and matches neither builds `x_view`,
discards it, and falls through to a path that uses the original `x`.

This moves the copy into the two branches that use it. The discarded value is
dead, so every path that consumed `x_view` still receives exactly the same
tensor.

## Results

Kimi-K3 FP4, 8x MI355X, TP8, concurrency 1, MTP depth 6, 384K-token context.
The layer that hits this is `f_b_proj` at **m=7, n=1536, k=128**: `k % 8 == 0`
passes the gate, `(m == 1 or m > 8)` is false, `m % 4 == 0` is false. Its input
is a 128-column slice of a 6284-wide projection output, so it is row-strided
and the copy is real work rather than a no-op.

BF16 `direct_copy_kernel_cuda`, same image and context, 6-step decode window:

| | per step | cost |
|---:|---:|---:|
| before | 73.0 | 0.3609 ms/step |
| after | 4.0 | 0.0218 ms/step |
| **removed** | **69.0** | **0.339 ms/step** |

69 removed per step is exactly one per KDA layer. Each moved 1,792 bytes for
about 4.8 us, so the cost was almost entirely launch overhead rather than
bandwidth. The 4 per step that remain are unrelated int64 index copies.

## How the copy was attributed

Not by reading the source — two earlier guesses from source were wrong. The
evidence is from profiles:

1. The kernel template is `gpu_kernel_impl_nocast<...(c10::BFloat16)>`, i.e. a
   same-dtype layout copy, not a dtype cast.
2. Fingerprinting neighbours in the kernel timeline put 420 of 438 copies
   directly between two Tensile GEMMs.
3. Re-running with CUDA graphs disabled kept all 438 copies, so they are not
   inserted by compilation. Every one then resolves through its `cpu_op`
   parents to:

   ```
   aten::copy_ <- aten::clone <- aten::contiguous <- vllm::rocm_unquantized_gemm
   ```

   414 of 414 attributed, 69 per step.
4. The control-flow arithmetic on the actual shape confirms both inner
   branches are false, so the copy is discarded.

A competing hypothesis — that Inductor inserted the copy because the custom op
carries no layout tag — was tested on GPU by tagging the op
`torch.Tag.flexible_layout`, and rejected: the count stayed at 73.0 per step.

## Correctness

No FLOPs change and no numerics change. The removed value was never read on
the affected path; on the two paths that do read it, the same
`x.reshape(-1, x.size(-1)).contiguous()` is still evaluated before use.

```
ruff check vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py       All checks passed!
ruff format --check vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py   1 file already formatted
```

## Why this is not a duplicate

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "rocm_unquantized_gemm"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "skinny gemm contiguous"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "wvSplitK contiguous copy"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "rocm unquantized gemm x_view"
```

No open PR touches this function.

## Who is affected

No flag changes are needed to pick this up. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM`
defaults to `True`, so a stock ROCm deployment is already on the affected
path; the configuration measured above sets nothing related to it.

The waste occurs when the broad outer gate passes and both narrow inner
conditions miss:

| condition | |
| --- | --- |
| `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM` | default `True` |
| `on_gfx9() or on_gfx1x()` | true on gfx950 (MI355X) |
| `x.dtype in [fp16, bf16]` | true for these activations |
| `k % 8 == 0` | 128 % 8 == 0 |
| `skinny_operands_compatible` | contiguous weight and bias |
| **inner:** `(m == 1 or m > 8) and 0 < n <= 5` | **false** at m=7, n=1536 |
| **inner:** `m % 4 == 0 and n == 1 and ...` | **false** at m=7, n=1536 |

Two consequences worth stating plainly, so the scope is not overread:

- A model whose GEMM shapes *do* match an inner branch was always consuming
  `x_view`, so there is nothing to remove and no change is expected.
- Anyone running with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0` never entered this block
  and is unaffected.

The copy is only real work when the input is non-contiguous. Here it is: the
`f_b_proj` input is a 128-column slice of a 6284-wide projection output. A
shape that passes the gate with an already-contiguous input pays a cheaper
no-op rather than a full copy.

## End-to-end (side note)

Deliberately last, and not the claim being made. 0.339 ms/step is roughly 1.5%
of a 23.5 ms decode step at this operating point, which is close to the
run-to-run spread we measure on this workload (~0.8%), and end-to-end
throughput also depends on the tuning of the surrounding GEMMs and attention
kernels. The removed copy count above is the honest result.

The benefit is not specific to Kimi-K3: any ROCm model whose GEMM shapes pass
the `use_skinny` gate while missing both inner conditions pays this today.

---

AI assistance was used for this change (Claude Opus 5). The measurements were
run by the submitter on MI355X hardware, and every changed line was reviewed by
the submitter.

title: [Qwen4Exp][ROCm] PLE n-gram table CPU offload
body:
## Purpose
- Enable `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` on the AMD/ROCm path: keep the Qwen4Exp PLE n-gram table in pinned host memory, read through a UVA view on the GPU.
- Free VRAM so `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (FP8 table ~51 GiB) / `Inferact/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (bf16 table ~102 GiB) serve on one MI300X with the table entirely in host RAM.
- Keep the pinned lookup behind a custom op (`qwen4_exp_amd_ple_ngram_embedding_pinned`) with `mutates_args=["output"]` so the large embedding weight is never materialized by `torch.compile` (Inductor autotuning builds a bf16 copy of the table during compile, which OOMs on AMD setups without enough VRAM) and the op survives aot_autograd/Inductor.
- Move the PLE embedding storage classes to `qwen4_exp/common` so the AMD and NVIDIA paths share one implementation (NVIDIA re-exports).
- Relax the PLE enable gate to `is_cuda_alike()` so ROCm is accepted, matching the existing NVIDIA default (`VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` defaults on for both; `=0` opts out). Also, my local testing shows little to no performance loss for PLE offload while saving a good chunk of VRAM for more KV cache.
- Why this is not duplicating existing PRs: 
  - #54371 (merged — source of the UVA offload code, ported here)
  - #55040 (AMD FP8 PLE, different approach: FP8 storage + forward dequant vs load-time bf16 fold; no offload/prefetch)
  - #55334 / #54070 / #54129 (nvidia + mmap — complementary).
- AI assistance: developed with opencode+deepseek-v4-flash+vllm; the submitting human reviewed every changed line and ran the tests/evals.

## Test Plan
- `uvx --from ruff==0.14.0 ruff check <changed files>`; `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (incl. mypy).
- `python -m pytest tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py -q` on ROCm (MI300X) — 52 passed, including compile and cudagraph-capture regression tests for the pinned lookup op.
- Offload-vs-device correctness: same prompt with `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0/1`, top-8 logprobs bit-identical (max diff 0.0).
- Eval: 1× MI300X, `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`, `--max-model-len 262144`, table pinned (weight_device=cpu), CPU KV offload tier.
- Offload ON vs OFF head-to-head (8192 ctx, identical engine): prefill TTFT, decode, and burst are equal within noise; the offload's value is VRAM, not speed.
- An async side-stream prefetch variant was prototyped and measured on the clean config (64k-token non-repeating prefill, default cudagraphs): TTFT difference was a wash vs the synchronous lookup and decode was identical, so this PR ships the synchronous version.

## Test Result
- 52/52 PLE tests pass on ROCm; offload-vs-device logprobs max diff 0.0; "17*23" → 391.
- Needle-in-haystack at 105k and 209k tokens recalled exactly; GPU KV pool 1.57M tokens (6.0× for 262144) on one MI300X.
- Perf: offload ON vs OFF at 8192 — TTFT (6144-token prefill) 0.33s vs 0.33s, decode 8.8 vs 8.9 tok/s (eager) / 87 vs 86 tok/s (default cudagraphs at 262144), 8-way burst 2.4s vs 2.4s. No measurable offload cost.

---

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

title: [DSpark] Support PP prefill with KV transfer (disaggregated serving)
body:
## What

DSpark pipeline-parallel support, end to end: **aggregated (in-flight-batching) serving with PP targets** and **prefill on a pipeline-parallel producer with KV transfer** (PD-disaggregated serving).

This PR is self-contained: it re-applies #56956 (reverted in #58484 for further streamlining) and builds the PD producer path on top. Happy to iterate on the streamlining with you, @njhill.

Aggregated IFB PP (re-applied #56956):

- `PPHandler` broadcasts the last rank's sampled tokens (and draft tokens, for spec decode) to earlier stages on a side stream; earlier stages apply them `pp_size` steps later in a deferred post-update.
- The deferred post-update Triton kernel is pre-compiled during warmup with the exact serving specialization (int32 `idx_mapping`, 16-byte-aligned `num_sampled`/`num_rejected` via a padded combined buffer) — a mid-serving compile there would deadlock on the in-flight broadcast NCCL kernel.
- DSv4 router: pad the top-k buffer so non-last stages can drop EAGLE read-ahead rows.

PD prefill-only producer (this PR on top):

- `SpeculativeConfig.target_kv_transfer_config` + `is_dspark_prefill_only()`; NIXL is rejected for this mode (it cannot describe packed per-layer KV regions; Mooncake works).
- The scheduler narrows `use_eagle` (and eagle block-drop) for the prefill-only producer so it never does the EAGLE-style read-ahead.
- `DFlashSpeculator.materialize_context_kv()`: precompute and store draft context KV without drafting; the model runner calls it in place of `propose()` on the producer and skips draft-side rejection sampling, drafter graph capture, and EPLB registration there. The preparation half is shared with `propose()` via `_prepare_draft_inputs()`; on the aggregated path the context-K/V store stays graph-aware as introduced by #57632 (merged here), while the producer stores eagerly (it captures no draft graph).
- The DSv4 draft in this mode builds only the attention submodule needed for prefill (`context_kv_only`) — avoiding transient MoE expert allocation — and loads just the context-KV weights (the merged `context_wkv_proj` plus per-layer `kv_norm`).

Kimi-K3 DSpark additionally relies on the TritonMLA causal multi-token fix from #51065 (merged; included in this branch's base; verified on SM120).

Split from #53577 (reviewer request).

## Tests

- `tests/config/test_dspark_prefill_only.py` (13 tests: mode detection, connector guard, last-stage drafter helper).
- `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py` — broadcast/padding + the warmup-serving specialization match (`_post_update_kernel`).
- `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py` — input-prep kernel behavior incl. `context_only`.
- `pytest tests/config/test_dspark_prefill_only.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py -q` → 22 passed on this tree; pre-commit green.

## Model evaluation

Validated end-to-end on the pre-split stack (#53577 lineage): DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 DSpark PD disaggregation with PP on both sides — prefill PP2×TP2 (prefill-only DSpark producer) + decode PP2×TP2 with DSpark, Mooncake KV transfer (TCP transport): GSM8K strict-match **0.9447** (1319 samples, stderr 0.0063). This is exactly the P-PP + D-PP DSpark combination previously reported to produce garbled output.

This rebuild rebases that stack onto current main (including the #57632 context-K/V graph-capture refactor and the #58484 revert of #56956, which this PR re-applies); the rebase keeps the aggregated-path behavior and changes no model numerics. Re-validation of the both-PP PD GSM8K on this exact tree is in progress and will be reported here.

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR.

title: [Perf][Kernel] Vectorized flat abs-max for dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization
body:
## Purpose

This PR speeds up the abs-max pass of `dynamic_scaled_fp8_quant` (per-tensor dynamic FP8 quantization) in `csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/common.cu`. It is the activation quant on every MoE layer of a model served with `--quantization fp8`, and it had never been performance-tuned.

I went in after reading #44173, which took the same kind of kernel (block-per-row, shared-memory tree reduction, scalar loads) and rewrote it as warp shuffles plus vector loads. This kernel had the same shape of problem, so I applied the same approach and measured what it actually buys.

**What was there before**

`segmented_max_reduction_strided` launched one block per token, did one scalar load per element, reduced through a 256-entry shared-memory tree with a `__syncthreads` per level, and issued one atomic per token. For a decode batch of 32 tokens, that is 32 blocks on a 132-SM GPU. For a 65536-token prefill it is 65536 atomics to one address.

**What this PR does**

- For contiguous input, the abs-max is a flat grid-stride kernel over 16-element vectors (32 B loads for bf16, 64 B for fp32). The reduction is a `__shfl_xor_sync` butterfly within each warp and one shared-memory exchange across warps, so a single barrier. The grid is sized from the vector count and capped at 8 blocks per SM, so a small batch gets exactly the blocks it needs and a large one loops. One atomic per block instead of one per token.
- Strided or unaligned input keeps the one-block-per-token kernel, now with vectorized loads (`vectorize_read_with_alignment`) and the same shuffle reduction in place of the tree.
- The quantize pass that follows is unchanged.

**Numerics**

Output is bit-for-bit identical to `main`. The per-element operations are unchanged (`fmaxf` for the abs-max, the same `scaled_fp8_conversion` for the quantize). `fmaxf` is order-invariant, and dividing by a positive constant is monotonic, so regrouping the max across threads, warps, or blocks cannot change any scale or any output byte. I verified this empirically rather than relying on the argument; see below. No API change. Strided rows and all dtypes behave as before.

**Not a duplicate.** #41115 (open since May, merge conflicts, no review) tunes block sizes on the per-token kernel and does not touch the per-tensor path. #55330 targets the per-token-group kernel and #45428 the fused RMSNorm quant kernel.

**Next work.** Once this is approved and merged, I plan a follow-up PR for the per-token kernel in the same file, which reuses the reduction helpers added here.

## Test Plan

- **Bitwise equivalence.** Built `main` and this branch on the same box. Dumped the quantized bytes and scales on CPU-seeded inputs for bf16 and fp32, M in {1, 7, 64, 512, 4096, 16384}, hidden in {17, 1024, 1025, 2048, 4096, 5137, 7168, 8192, 16384, 32768}, and three row layouts (contiguous, misaligned by 8 elements, aligned but padded by 16). Compared with `torch.equal`.
- **Unit tests.** `tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py`, plus a new strided-input test that forces the fallback kernel at both alignments.
- **Performance.** H100 80 GB HBM3, driver 580, CUDA 13.0.3, torch 2.13.0+cu130. `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph`, median of the full op including the memset and both kernels, so this is what a caller sees.
- **End to end.** Qwen3-30B-A3B with `--quantization fp8`, `vllm bench throughput` and `vllm bench latency`, main vs this branch on the same box.

Commands run:

```bash
pre-commit run --files csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/fp8/common.cu tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_fp8_quant.py -q
vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 2048 --dataset-name random --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --num-prompts 512
vllm bench latency --model Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --quantization fp8 --max-model-len 2048 --input-len 1024 --output-len 128 --batch-size 32 --num-iters 10
```

## Test Result

- Bitwise: **1080 cases identical, 0 mismatched**, bytes and scales.
- Tests: **249 passed**.

**Per-tensor, bf16, `main` vs this PR**

| M | hidden | main (us) | PR (us) | speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16 | 4096 | 8.21 | 5.61 | 1.46x |
| 16 | 8192 | 11.36 | 6.01 | 1.89x |
| 512 | 4096 | 9.58 | 7.39 | 1.30x |
| 512 | 7168 | 12.60 | 8.79 | 1.43x |
| 4096 | 4096 | 48.95 | 30.51 | 1.60x |
| 4096 | 7168 | 85.17 | 55.27 | 1.54x |
| 16384 | 4096 | 187.22 | 115.96 | 1.61x |
| 16384 | 7168 | 312.94 | 196.30 | 1.59x |
| 65536 | 4096 | 715.88 | 436.15 | 1.64x |
| 65536 | 8192 | 1378.42 | 866.10 | 1.59x |

Geomean **1.39x** across bf16 and fp32, M in {16, 512, 4096, 16384, 65536}, hidden in {2048, 4096, 7168, 8192}. Range 1.11x to 1.89x. At large M, the op now moves about 3.0 TB/s of real traffic (two reads and one write), which is where it should sit on this GPU.

**End to end: Qwen3-30B-A3B with online FP8**

`--quantization fp8` quantizes activations per-tensor dynamically, and on a MoE model, the expert input of every layer goes through this kernel. Same H100, `vllm bench throughput`, random dataset, 1024 in / 128 out, 512 prompts, three interleaved runs per build after a warm compile cache:

| build | tokens/s (3 runs) | mean | stdev |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| main | 43793, 43706, 43835 | 43778 | 66 |
| this PR | 45154, 44810, 44965 | 44977 | 172 |

**+2.7% throughput**, with run-to-run spread under 0.4%. Batch latency (`vllm bench latency`, batch 32, 1024 in / 128 out): 1.876 s vs 1.843 s avg, about 1.8% lower.

The gain lands where expected: with the compiler fusing this model's per-token quant sites into RMSNorm, the per-tensor abs-max pass on the MoE expert inputs is the only kernel this PR changes that runs in the trace. Model output is unaffected since the kernel is bitwise identical.

I used Claude Code for this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests and benchmarks above myself.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable layer-aware CSA2 multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
body:
## Purpose DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has three attention layer shapes: full CSA2 layers (2/8/14/20) run SWA + compressor + indexer and build a new global KV cache with their own Top-K indices; reindex CSA2 layers (24/28/32/36) run SWA + indexer only, re-scoring Top-K over an earlier layer's global KV cache; all other layers are dense or pure SWA. The shared v4.1 pipeline overlaps the full CSA2 layers with **three** fork/join pairs per step (input projections; Q/SWA-insert vs compressor; indexer vs cache-insert) and the reindex layers with one. On ROCm each fork/join is a HIP event pair per side stream, so the multi-stream launch cost outweighs the overlap benefit there. --- This PR gives the ROCm attention layer a layer-type-aware scheme with exactly one fork/join per step: **Full CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_full`)**: one 3-stream fork right after the input norm. - default stream: fused wqa+wkv → q/kv split+norm → wq_b → fused qnorm/RoPE/SWA-insert; - aux stream 0: the compressor chain (kv_score GEMM → save/compress/norm → RoPE-quant cache insert); - aux stream 1: indexer `weights_proj`. After the single join, the indexer K write (`_produce_k`, whose `wk` consumes the aux-0 latent) and the query path (`forward_q`, whose wq_b consumes the default-stream qr) run serially, followed by the indexer op and sparse MLA. **Reindex CSA2 layers (`_forward_csa2_reindex`)**: the input projections run serially first (the query path consumes qr, so overlapping the weight projection is not worth it), then one 2-stream fork overlaps the SWA q path with the indexer query path. **Dense layers**: fully serial (`aux_stream_list` disabled). --- A new shared helper `execute_in_parallel_default_first` (in `vllm/utils/multi_stream_utils.py`) mirrors `execute_in_parallel` but enqueues the default chain before the aux chains — the default chain is the longest, so starting it first shortens the step tail while the aux streams still only wait on the pre-fork default-stream work. The fork is gated exactly like the shipped v4.0 multi-stream gate (#51794/#56853): it only runs where the fork/join becomes static graph edges (inside capture, or with non-dict metadata such as the profile run); everywhere else — including MRV1, which keeps its wide eager region (#51430) — the layer falls back to the fully sequential base pipeline. The CUDA/NVIDIA path is untouched except for a behavior-neutral base refactor: the v4.1 indexer's query path is extracted into `DeepseekV4Indexer.forward_q`, still driven unchanged by the base `forward` (`_produce_k` keeps its private name). This is not a duplicate of #51794/#56853, which cover v4.0: v4.1-flash has a different topology (the indexer derives K from the kv-source compressor's latent, with no indexer-local compressor), so the overlap must differ per layer type. ## Trace Comparison (Take conc=4 as an example) **With regard to CSA2 layers with compressor and indexer (layer_id=2/8/14/20):** Before: > The default NV path launches multi-stream 3 times per layer, which is inefficient on ROCm path (multi-stream cost > overlap benefit). After (**20.76%** faster than the old pattern): --- **With regard to CSA2 layers only with indexer (layer_id=24/28/32/36):** Before: > No need to overlap indexer weight projection, since the benefit (4 μs) < the multi-stream cost (5 μs + 6 μs = 11 μs). Instead, we prefer to overlap SWA process and indexer process. After (**11.90%** faster than the old pattern): ## Test Plan Benchmark with SA InferenceX `8k1k` workload with server launch commands below: ```bash export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 export AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 GPU_COUNT=4 export HF_HOME=/shared/models vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 8333 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --moe-backend aiter \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --max-num-seqs 128 \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --disable-uvicorn-access-log \ --no-swa-bounded-replay \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \ 2>&1 | tee "${OUTDIR}/server.log" ``` Accuracy test with `gsm8k` dataset using `lm_eval`: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://0.0.0.0:8333/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=10,max_gen_toks=2048,timeout=60000,tokenized_requests=False \ --batch_size auto \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --output_path . 2>&1 | tee -a eval.log ``` > [!NOTE] > All tests based on latest `nightly-rocm100` image. ## Test Result ### Benchmark By the way, note that the e2e benefit could be small, since there are onlt **8** layers that we can optimize (overlap), while other layers always execute serially. | Conc | Version | Output token throughput (tok/s) | Change | Mean TTFT (ms) | Change | Mean TPOT (ms) | Change | | ---: | :------ | ------------------------------: | :-----: | -------------: | :------: | -------------: | :-----: | | 1 | main | 114.47 | — | 392.61 | — | 8.32 | — | | 1 | this PR | 117.28 | 2.45% ↑ | 266.06 | 32.23% ↓ | 8.25 | 0.84% ↓ | | 4 | main | 381.72 | — | 348.33 | — | 9.86 | — | | 4 | this PR | 386.47 | 1.24% ↑ | 331.76 | 4.76% ↓ | 9.76 | 1.01% ↓ | | 16 | main | 1018.13 | — | 496.96 | — | 14.73 | — | | 16 | this PR | 1018.69 | 0.06% ↑ | 495.02 | 0.39% ↓ | 14.73 | 0.00% | | 64 | main | 1912.44 | — | 1165.33 | — | 31.71 | — | | 64 | this PR | 1920.10 | 0.40% ↑ | 1160.00 | 0.46% ↓ | 31.59 | 0.38% ↓ | In summary, the performance data indicates that this PR provides consistent throughput gains and latency reductions without introducing a regression in the tested metrics. The most noticeable benefit is at low concurrency, while at higher concurrency (conc=16 and 64) the changes are comparatively small, suggesting that the optimization has limited additional impact once the system becomes heavily loaded. ### Accuracy Test Main: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| This PR: |Tasks|Version| Filter |n-shot| Metric | |Value | |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9363|± |0.0067| | | |strict-match | 5|exact_match|↑ |0.9371|± |0.0067| ---

title: [ROCm][MLA] Add an AITER ASM round-robin decode route for DCP multi-token verify
body:
## Purpose

**Makes the AITER ASM MLA decode path reachable when decode context parallelism (DCP) is combined with speculative decoding on ROCm. Today it is not reachable at all in that configuration.**

#51705 added DCP multi-token verify through the *segmented* route: it expands a verify group into one single-query row per token and carries the causal window in per-row lengths, running the Triton `mla_decode_fwd` kernel. Because a spec-decode step always has `qlen = 1 + num_speculative_tokens > 1`, that route is taken for **all** of decode, so turning on DCP together with spec decode silently costs you the entire AITER ASM MLA path.

This PR adds a second, **additive** route that keeps those steps on the ASM path: the AITER round-robin (`cprr`) decode. It keeps the verify group as one row of `qlen` queries and reconstructs each token's **global** position in-kernel from a global per-request page indptr (`g_kv_indptr`) plus `cp_rank`/`cp_world_size`, so causality is applied inside the kernel rather than materialised on the host.

|  | segmented (existing) | asm cprr (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| batch shape | N rows × 1 query | 1 row × N queries |
| causality | per-row lengths, host-built | in-kernel, from global positions |
| kernel | Triton `mla_decode_fwd` | AITER fp8 ASM `..._cprr_ps` |
| KV reads | ~1 per verify token | once, amortised over the block |

The route is selected per KV cache group by `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` (registered in `vllm/envs.py`): `asm` (default) or `segmented`, optionally restricted to listed DCP-gathered head counts, e.g. `segmented:64` keeps a 64-head draft on Triton while a 96-head target stays on ASM. A speculative target and its draft gather different head counts, so they can be routed independently.

### Where the route is reachable

Four conditions, so it is enabled only where it works and is needed:

- **gfx950.** The `cprr` kernels are built only for it: `hsa/gfx942/mla` and `hsa/gfx1250/mla` carry no `cprr` rows, so elsewhere the lookup would fail at the first verify step instead of falling back.
- **Multi-token decode** (`speculative_config is not None`). Single-token decode is already served. Enabling the route there would still override the attention head count to the padded native width on every step, for no benefit.
- **`decode_context_parallel_size > 1`**, and **`cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 1`**, the same restriction the segmented gate carries.

Within that, the head-count rules: the ASM kernel exists only at the native DCP-gathered counts `(16, 32, 64, 128)`; other counts pad up to the next native one (96 to 128), and a count above the largest native is refused at build time rather than silently leaving the ASM path.

### Causality

`causal` is forwarded to the kernel. AITER defaults it to `True`, so a non-causal group (a DSpark draft attends its whole block) would otherwise get the masked kernel and see only tokens up to its own index. The non-causal `cprr` kernels exist (`msk0_lse_cprr`); they have to be asked for.

`qlen == 1` is already correct on the plain kernel, since a decode row sees every local token.

**`qlen == 2` raises.** There is no `cprr` kernel below 3, and the plain kernel applies causality on *local* indices over a round-robin shard, which is silently wrong rather than an error. The constructor rejects a configured qlen of 2, but `max_qo_len` is a per-batch value: the scheduler can clamp a running spec request to 2 under a larger configured threshold, so the per-step path checks it too.

### Route selection is fail-fast

The head-count filter rejects empty entries (`segmented:,`, `asm:64,`) and non-positive counts (`asm:0`). Both previously parsed to a filter that matches nothing, which applies the route to *every* grou
p: the opposite of what was asked, silently.

### KV split cap

This PR also passes `max_split_per_batch` through the DCP MLA metadata, set to
the device CU count. At batch 1 there are few query rows against tens of
thousands of KV rows, so splitting the KV axis is the only parallelism
available. On gfx950 at batch 1, qlen 15, 128 heads: 32 splits takes 456 us,
256 takes 103 us. It is a maximum rather than a fixed count, so it stops
mattering once the batch itself fills the device.

`reduce_partial_map` is allocated with the cap applied, so the sizing call and
the runtime build both have to see the same value. They read the same builder
attribute.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Additive.** None of the five `_asm_dcp_verify_*` symbols exist upstream; the segmented route is untouched and stays reachable via the env var. With `decode_context_parallel_size == 1` nothing here i
s reachable at all.
- **No AITER changes required.** Verified by reverting our local AITER patches and re-running the whole suite, with identical results (see Test Result). We have a separate AITER change that tightens the reduce-scratch bound when a cap is supplied; it is a pure memory optimisation, is inert without a caller that passes a cap to the *sizing* call, and can land in either order. Until it does, this PR siz
es that scratch generously.
- **This is an enablement change, not a tuning change**, which is why the headline is a capability rather than a percentage. Because the route is selected at runtime, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm` vs `segmented` compares the two routes on an identical build, model and workload, so reviewers can reproduce the comparison on their own hardware. We are not quoting an end-to-end percentage yet because we want a same-config A/B we can fully stand behind rather than a number carried over from a differently-configured run; we will follow up with one.
## Test Plan

```bash
# new: routing / selection (pure CPU, runs anywhere)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py

# new: numerics (real metadata builder + real ASM kernel; needs gfx950 + AITER)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py

# regression: the pre-existing AITER MLA suite
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` (31 tests, CPU) pins the *decisions*: every accepted form of the env var plus both error paths, head-count selection including the 96 → 128 pad and the unservable case, per-group routing, the interleave restriction, and the `qlen` floor.

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py` (4 tests, GPU) is the correctness gate. It drives the real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.build()` and the real ASM kernel, simulating the DCP ranks one after another in a single process. That is sound because this path is collective-free: the query all-gather happens in the layer, strictly before `forward_mqa`, so `cp_rank` only selects which residue class of global positions the shard holds. It asserts:

- each shard against an exact torch reference over the global positions it holds, at 128 gathered heads (native) **and** 96 (padded to 128);
- that the LSE merge of all shards reproduces full-context attention;
- that `asm_decode_num_heads` is set, so a silent fall-out to the segmented or Triton path fails loudly instead of passing quietly;
- **positive control**: handing shard `r`'s pages to the kernel while telling it that it is rank `r+1` must blow the error up. Without this a green run would prove nothing, because a kernel that ignored global positions still produces plausible-looking output.

No model weights are downloaded: the MLA dims come from the DeepSeek-R1 *config* (already used by the existing MLA tests) with only the head count overridden, and the parallel groups are single-process stubs.

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` fakes the builder and the decode metadata with `SimpleNamespace`, so the fields this PR adds to the real classes are added there too, set to the route-off values. Those cases therefore keep exercising the segmented/persistent path they were written for.

## Test Result

All on gfx950 (MI355X), ROCm 7.2.3.

| file | collected | needs |
|---|---:|---|
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` | 39 | nothing, pure CPU |                                                                                                                                            | `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py` | 4 | AITER on gfx950 |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` | 59 | nothing, pure CPU |

No regressions in the pre-existing AITER MLA suite.

Forcing `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=segmented` turns the GPU tests red, so they are genuinely pinned to the route under test.

**What the tests do not cover.** The numerics file is the only coverage of the builder and decode paths, and it skips without gfx950, so on a runner without one a change to the per-step qlen gate, the `cprr` kwargs, or the `causal` forward fails nothing. It also fixes `QLEN = 5`, `causal=True` and `non_causal_multi_token_decode=False`, so qlen 1, qlen 2 and the non-causal path are not exercised anywhere. The CPU files cover the env parsing, the reachability gate and the head-count mapping.

**Numerics.** Per-shard maximum relative error against the exact torch reference, 8 DCP shards, fp8 KV:

```
shard 0..7:  1.32e-02 … 1.87e-02
merged vs full-context reference: 1.18e-02
```

against an fp8-e4m3 error floor of ~6.2e-2 (3 mantissa bits). Gates are relative, because with fp8 the error floor scales with output magnitude and an absolute gate would just be a magnitude gate.

**AITER requirement.** This needs an AITER build that ships the round-robin MLA
decode kernels, added in ROCm/aiter#4521. No AITER change is required beyond
that.

title: [Rust Frontend] Add MiniCPM5 tool parser support
body:
**Incremental review:** [Files changed](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57096/files) against `main`.

## Summary

Implement the `minicpm5` tool-parser parity item for the Rust frontend from #44280. This updates the existing PR rather than opening a duplicate.

Add native MiniCPM5 XML-style function-call parsing and register it with Rust chat serving. Support non-streaming and streaming output, arbitrary decoded chunk boundaries, multiple calls, schema-aware parameter conversion/validation, wrapped parameters, aliases, and invalid/truncated-input fallback. Streaming emits each call ID/name once and reconstructs valid JSON arguments.

Add four real-model OpenAI E2E cases to the existing tool-use suite: single/multiple calls × synchronous/streaming responses. Reuse its model configuration and fixtures, and add a MiniCPM5 command to the existing Rust frontend tool-use CI job.

title: [Perf] Batch Mamba2 prefill SSM state saves, removing GPU<->CPU syncs
body:
## Purpose

`MambaMixer2.conv_ssm_forward` saves the block-aligned SSM states of each prefill sequence in a Python loop over `num_prefills`. #43107 moved the four scalar reads that loop needs out of it and left a `# TODO avoid sync here?` there. This removes the loop, so those four `.tolist()` calls go with it and no GPU<->CPU sync is left on this path. The writes of all sequences become one pair of index tensors and a single indexed copy.

The write count has to be a host value, so it comes from the metadata builder as `num_state_writes_p`, derived from CPU data the way #51738's `_prefill_cpu_metadata` does — the chunk metadata already depends on that same equality. One other detail: `torch.repeat_interleave(x, counts)` reads its output size off the device unless `output_size=` is passed, so both calls pass it.

## Test plan

New case in `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_update_block_table.py` for the host-vs-device equality this relies on; `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py` already covers the path itself. Offline, the batched version is bit-identical to the deleted loop over 250 randomized workloads (4,766 state writes) spanning block/chunk ratios 1–4 and 1–32 prefills.

## Test result

Serving, measured on 2026-09-22 with `vllm serve` and `vllm bench serve` on current main (`4868312128`), `mamba_cache_mode=all`, prefix caching on. The client keeps 64 requests in flight, prompts are random tokens of a fixed length, and each request generates 8 tokens. Each arm ran on 2 fresh servers with 3 benches per server, alternating baseline and patched. Both GPUs use `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`.

| GPU | model | input len | TTFT median | TTFT p99 | req/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H100 | Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 | 8192 | 8387 → 7211 ms (−14.0%) | 9473 → 8002 ms (−15.5%) | 6.7 → 7.9 (+17.7%) |
| A100-80GB | granite-4.0-h-tiny | 1536 | 1064 → 862 ms (−19.0%) | 2600 → 2081 ms (−20.0%) | 24.6 → 30.5 (+24.1%) |
| H100 | granite-4.0-h-tiny | 1536 | 648 → 629 ms (−3.0%) | 1556 → 1514 ms (−2.7%) | 41.0 → 42.1 (+2.7%) |

The gain depends on what the step is waiting on. In the first two rows the GPU is the bottleneck and the CPU runs ahead of it. Each sync then drains the launch queue and the GPU idles until the CPU catches up. I sampled `nvidia-smi` during the benches, and GPU utilization went from about 80% to 100% in both of those rows. In the last row the engine core sits at 100% of one CPU core and the GPU at about 55% in both arms, so the syncs cost little there and the change is within run-to-run noise. The two ranges overlap in that row and do not overlap in the other two.

Nemotron needs 8192-token prompts here because `mamba_cache_mode=all` resolves its mamba block to 2176 tokens, and the loop only saves states for the full blocks before a prompt's last block.

Offline prefill batch on the same commit, A100-80GB, `granite-4.0-h-tiny`, 256 × 1536-token prompts, `mamba_cache_mode=all`, alternating baseline and patched, 3 runs each:

| version | wall (s) |
|---|---|
| baseline | 9.905 ± 0.253 |
| patched | 8.525 ± 0.052 |

**13.9% end to end.** The two arms do not overlap: the fastest baseline run (9.717 s) is still slower than the slowest patched run (8.582 s). A separate pinned-batch run on the same GPU (greedy, 4 runs) gives the same output token ids and the same scheduling counters with and without the patch, so the win is host-side rather than a scheduling difference. This is measured after #43107, #51738 and #52506 landed in the same files.

## Notes

Developed with Claude Code. I reviewed every line and ran the tests myself.

Duplicate check: the loop, the TODO and the four `.tolist()` calls are all still on `main`, and no open or merged PR batches this loop or removes these syncs. The nearest is #51738, a different sync in the same file.

title: [Quantization] Layer re-quantization for linear layers through online quantization API (MXFP8 -> FP8 PTPC showcase)
body:
## Disclosure

AI assistance was used. The changes were reviewed and tested manually.

## Purpose

This PR allows re-quantizing linear layers to a different precision using online quantization API, as long as the `dequantize_weight` method for relevant `LinearMethodBase` subclass is implemented.

Similar features have been requested previously in specialized cases:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51274

and this feature exists on sglang side https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28291 / https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29328.

Addresses the third item of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/52167. This PR is adapted from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48427, co-authored by @tanpinsiang.

This change lets `--quantization-config.linear fp8_per_channel` convert selected serialized ModelOpt MXFP8 linears to FP8 PTPC at load time.

The original checkpoint quantization config remains responsible for unselected linears and MoE.

The composition is handled by the existing `resolve_quant_method`, so model implementations continue to receive their original checkpoint quantization config type.

Quantization methods expose an optional `dequantize_weight` method, that:

- raises `NotImplementedError` by default, or
- dequantizes the quant method weights if implemented.

This draft implements it only for `ModelOptMxFp8LinearMethod`.

Such `dequantize_weight` methods implementation can be shared across model producers (quark, modelopt, compressed-tensors, etc.) based on weight quant key, no model producer-specific code should be required.

## Test Plan

```bash
vllm serve mmangkad/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-MXFP8 --quantization-config.linear "fp8_per_channel"
```

title: [Attention][CPU] Run Zen CPU decoder prefill on zentorch SDPA
body:
## Purpose

Route **decoder prefill / extend** on the vLLM CPU backend through `zentorch_sdpa` on Zen CPUs, instead of always using the paged `cpu_attention_with_kv_cache` kernel.

Prefill has no need to gather K/V back out of the page table when the tokens for this step (and, for extends, the already-written cache) can be attended densely. Decode is unchanged: `query_len` at or below the reorder threshold still runs `cpu_attention_with_kv_cache`.

Dispatch:

- **Equal-length fresh prefills** (`query_len == seq_len` for every row): one `zentorch_sdpa.out(is_causal=True)` over a dense `[B, H, S, D]` batch.
- **Ragged fresh prefills and chunked extends**: one padded call with a bottom-right causal mask. Extends gather the cached prefix from the paged K/V cache.
- **Mixed batches**: the metadata builder requests a `[decode | extend | fresh prefill]` order, zentorch fills the prefill suffix, and the native kernel runs only the decode prefix with rebuilt scheduler metadata.

The path is used only for plain decoder self-attention in bf16/fp32 when `zentorch_sdpa` is registered. ALiBi, sliding window, logits softcap, attention sinks, FP8 KV cache, KV-sharing, encoder, and cross-attention stay native. The KV cache write is unchanged (`forward_includes_kv_cache_update = False`); this only skips the paged **read** for prefill rows.

This does not duplicate an in-tree CPU prefill SDPA path. It is the decoder-prefill counterpart of the Zen CPU encoder SDPA work. No `supported_models.md` / examples update: no new model, same CPU backend.

AI assistance was used to implement and review the change. The submitting author reviewed every line.

## Test Plan

On a Zen CPU with zentorch installed (so `torch.ops.zentorch.zentorch_sdpa` is registered):

```bash
# unit tests (skip cleanly on non-Zen / missing op)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_zen_cpu_prefill_sdpa.py -v

# existing CPU attention suite (decode / mixed / encoder must stay native-correct)

title: [Feature][MoE] Collect expert distributions with or without EPLB
body:
## Purpose

Add opt-in logical expert-routing statistics that work with or without Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB). Users can inspect which experts receive assignments without enabling expert rearrangement or changing the routing policy.

Rebased on September 23, 2026 onto public `main` at `f9ad9dd6b495f7492fa975e0ac48164b090d99ad`.

## User experience

Use one collection configuration in either mode:

```bash
# Observe without balancing.
vllm serve MODEL --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
    --expert-load-stats-config '{"enabled":true,"log_interval":1000,"output_dir":"./expert-load"}'

# Collect the same statistics while balancing.
vllm serve MODEL --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-eplb \
    --expert-load-stats-config '{"enabled":true,"log_interval":1000,"output_dir":"./expert-load"}'
```

The JSONL schema and logical expert identity do not change with EPLB. Dotted CLI options and the equivalent Python configuration are supported. Existing `--eplb-config` policy, recording windows, and balancedness logging keep their current meaning.

- Interval summaries: per-layer expert counts, assignment totals, maximum/mean, and unused experts.
- Optional bounded per-layer/per-iteration JSONL traces, with sampling and layer selection.
- Rank-local source-token ownership; no observability all-reduce/all-gather or Prometheus expert-label expansion.
- Logical routing skew is distinct from physical EP-rank balance. Replication can improve physical balance without changing logical selections.

## Implementation and scope

Instrument non-monolithic `BaseRouter` target-model routing. Without EPLB, use a histogram kernel; with EPLB, fuse logical counting into the existing mapping traversal while retaining separate logical counters and preserving physical counters/sampling. Persistent buffers support graph replay; two asynchronous export slots bound buffering and keep writer waits off the inference thread. Slow exports drop trace samples with an explicit counter, not summary counts.

Disabled collection allocates no tracker or device/export resources. Enabled collection has instrumentation and export costs; no performance result is claimed.

Iteration IDs are local target-forward counters, not synchronized DP steps. Target verification tokens are included even if subsequently rejected; draft forwards, warmup, dummy calls, padding, and shared experts are excluded. Initial support is CUDA/non-monolithic routing; unsupported paths such as custom/monolithic routers, LoRA, DBO/ubatching, CP, and elastic EP fail closed. See the feature documentation for the complete scope and ownership semantics.

## Rebase compatibility

Preserve main's new pipeline-parallel warmup broadcast guard alongside expert-statistics warmup suppression: neither synthetic token broadcasts nor warmup expert counts are enabled during startup. Update the existing MRV2 EPLB test fixture with the disabled-by-default collection configuration and assert that enabling EPLB alone does not create a statistics tracker. Collection options, output schema, and kernels are unchanged by this rebase.

## Related work

Searched open PRs/issues for expert distribution, histograms, load statistics, and independent collection. #43715 / #30696 concern physical per-rank EPLB metrics and Prometheus, rather than EPLB-independent logical-expert JSONL histograms. #41141 concerns offline expert placement; #56716 concerns the existing EPLB warmup recording lifecycle. This feature does not replace those changes.

## Test plan and results

- Changed-file `pre-commit run --from-ref f9ad9dd6b495f7492fa975e0ac48164b090d99ad --to-ref HEAD` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Previous GitHub runs were blocked by the contributor-verification policy before hosted pre-commit ran. The passing hook results above are local results; current-head hosted results are separate.
- Focused pytest targets: **78 passed, 21 skipped**:
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_expert_load_stats.py`
  - `tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py`
  - `tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py::test_expert_load_stats_cli`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_eplb.py`
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py`
- CPU run used a test-only device-type override for CLI default construction and the existing `skip_global_cleanup` marker via a temporary pytest plugin to avoid a local PyTorch accelerator-cleanup crash. Neither workaround is committed. CUDA tests were skipped, not passed.
- Coverage includes identical collection options with EPLB on/off, coexistence with routed-expert capture, logical token ownership, trace limits, summary resets, backpressure, and writer errors. Added CUDA tests cover exact histograms, graph replay, asynchronous export, and EPLB mapping/sampling preservation; they still need execution.
- Existing V1 worker CI collects the new test file. A synthetic kernel benchmark is provided without benchmark results.

Before ready-for-review promotion: run CUDA correctness/graph tests, distributed ownership checks, output-equivalence/model evaluation, and end-to-end overhead measurements. None of those GPU/serving results is claimed here.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, review, and tests. This is intentionally a draft for human line-by-line review and the remaining GPU/distributed validation.

title: [Refactor][Core] Use torch's device-agnostic streams and events in the V2 model runner
body:
## Purpose

The V2 model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/`) creates its copy streams and events as `torch.cuda.Stream` / `torch.cuda.Event`, switches streams with `torch.cuda.stream(...)`, and reads the current stream with `torch.cuda.current_stream()` in `async_utils`, `pp_utils`, `structured_outputs`, `spec_decode/utils`, `spec_decode/adaptive_verification` and the runner's `main_stream`. None of that code is CUDA-specific: it needs a stream, an event and the current stream of whatever accelerator torch is running on.

This PR switches those sites to torch's device-agnostic API: `torch.Stream(device=...)`, `torch.Event(device=..., blocking=True)`, `torch.accelerator.current_stream()`, and the existing lightweight `stream()` context manager in `async_utils`, which now uses `torch.accelerator.set_stream()`. On CUDA these resolve to the same objects, so in-tree behaviour is unchanged. `cudagraph_utils` and `ubatch_utils` keep `torch.cuda`, since graph capture and the cuBLAS handle are CUDA features.

Why: every non-CUDA runner today gets past these lines by aliasing `torch.cuda` process-wide. The in-tree XPU runner rebinds `torch.cuda.Stream`, `Event`, `graph` and `CUDAGraph` around `super().__init__()` (`vllm/v1/worker/xpu_model_runner.py`), the in-tree CPU runner installs `_StreamPlaceholder` / `_EventPlaceholder`, and vllm-ascend assigns twelve `torch.cuda.*` attributes to `torch.npu.*` with an empty `finally` (`vllm_ascend/worker/v2/utils.py`). The checklist to route these through the platform in #9268 has been open since 2024. Using the generic API removes the need for any routing: torch dispatches to the current accelerator.

Two small semantic notes for review:

- `copy_event.record()` inside a `with torch.cuda.stream(s):` block becomes `copy_event.record(s)`, which records on the same stream explicitly.
- `torch.Event(device=..., blocking=True)` is the generic spelling of `torch.cuda.Event(blocking=True)`; the timing events in `pp_utils` become `torch.Event(enable_timing=True)`.

## Test Plan

- `pre-commit run --files` on the six changed files (ruff, mypy, typos).
- The change is a rename of API surface on CUDA; the objects and their behaviour are the same. CI on this PR exercises the async output path, structured outputs, pipeline parallelism and speculative decoding.
- Downstream, the same change was run on a non-CUDA accelerator that implements `torch.Stream` / `torch.Event` and has no `torch.cuda`: async output, structured outputs, prompt logprobs, pooling, DP=2 and EAGLE/EAGLE3 speculative decoding end to end.

## Test Result

```
pre-commit run --files <6 files>   ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy-3.10, typos: Passed
git diff main..HEAD                6 files changed, 46 insertions(+), 42 deletions(-)
```

Downstream (v0.26.0 port of this change, non-CUDA accelerator): V2 e2e 6 passed, EAGLE + EAGLE3 2 passed.

Not run locally: the CUDA test suite (the development host has no GPU). A reviewer with a GPU should confirm that `torch.Event(device=..., blocking=True)` and `torch.accelerator.set_stream` behave as `torch.cuda.Event(blocking=True)` and `torch.cuda.set_stream` on the async output path; CI should cover this.

title: [Bugfix] Apply structured output on /v1/completions when the prompt never opens reasoning
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57726.

With a reasoning parser configured, a `/v1/completions` request carrying a
structured-output constraint comes back **unconstrained**, with a 200 and no
warning. The same request on the same model without `--reasoning-parser` is
constrained. `/v1/chat/completions` is unaffected.

## Root cause

`StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_start()` infers the initial reasoning
state from the prompt with a single question:

```python
if reasoner.is_reasoning_end(request.prompt_token_ids or []):
    return 0
structured_req.reasoning_ended = False
```

`BaseThinkingReasoningParser.is_reasoning_end()` scans backwards and returns
`False` on the start token, `True` on the end token, and falls through to
`return False` when it finds neither. That final line conflates two opposite
states:

| prompt | `is_reasoning_end` | meaning | current behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| ends with `<think>` | `False` | inside reasoning | wait for `</think>` — correct |
| contains `<think></think>` | `True` | reasoning closed | constrain now — correct |
| contains **neither** | `False` | never entered reasoning | wait forever — **bug** |

A raw completions prompt renders no chat template, so it is the third row. No
reasoning-end token will ever arrive, so the bitmask is never applied and the
model is unconstrained for the whole completion.

The same holds for the engine parser family: `ParserEngineReasoningAdapter`
inherits `ReasoningParser` and proxies the same properties, so both families
reach the gate through this one inference.

## The change

Ask the second question at the same place: does the prompt contain a reasoning
**start** marker at all? `ReasoningParser.reasoning_start_str` already exists
for this and the manager never consulted it.

A parser that exposes no start marker, or whose marker is absent from the
vocabulary, keeps today's behaviour — the helper returns `False` for "cannot
tell", so only a provable never-entered-reasoning prompt changes.

## Verification

Behaviour of the gate before and after, driven through the repo's own
`is_reasoning_end` source:

| prompt shape | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| chat, thinking on (ends `<think>`) | waits | waits |
| chat, thinking off (`<think></think>`) | constrained | constrained |
| chat mid-reasoning, long prompt | waits | waits |
| reasoning closed then reopened | waits | waits |
| reasoning closed, trailing content | constrained | constrained |
| **raw completions, no reasoning tokens** | **waits** | **constrained** |
| **raw completions, empty prompt** | **waits** | **constrained** |

Exactly the two raw-completions rows change; the five chat rows are untouched.
Parsers without a start marker are identical on all seven.

Tests added to `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py`,
parametrized over both backends:

- `test_constraint_applies_when_prompt_never_opens_reasoning` — a prompt that
  opens reasoning still waits, one that closes it is constrained, and one with
  no reasoning tokens is now constrained rather than free.
- `test_parser_without_start_marker_keeps_waiting` — the fallback stays on the
  previous behaviour.

Both fail on `main` for the no-reasoning-tokens case and pass with this change.

title: [Security] Cap Cohere2 Vision max_patches to prevent request-driven resource exhaustion
body:
## Summary

- Reject request-level `mm_processor_kwargs.max_patches` (including nested `images_kwargs.max_patches`) when the value is not a positive integer or exceeds the server-owned Cohere2 Vision cap.
- Treat the processor default, or operator `--mm-processor-kwargs`, as the authority for that cap so a client cannot raise the Hugging Face tile-enumeration budget.
- Add regression tests covering oversized, nested, non-integer, and in-range overrides, plus the operator-configured cap.

## Root Cause

Cohere2 Vision forwards per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` into Hugging Face `get_number_of_image_patches` / processor construction with no upper bound. The Transformers helper enumerates tile aspect ratios with nested loops bounded by `max_patches`, so a small valid image plus a large override (for example `max_patches=20000`) causes quadratic CPU work during multimodal preprocessing, before normal inference limits apply. Distinct values also miss the helper's small LRU cache.

## Fix

Two checks on the Cohere2 Vision processing path, using the server/model configuration as the cap:

1. **Validate in `get_hf_processor`** -- request kwargs are rejected before the HF processor is constructed or called, so `__call__` never sees an oversized `max_patches`.
2. **Validate in `get_num_patches`** -- the same bound is applied before `get_number_of_image_patches`, covering prompt-update and fallback patch-count paths.

Both flat `max_patches` and nested `images_kwargs.max_patches` are checked. Values must be integers in `[1, limit]`; `bool`, strings, floats, zero, and negatives are rejected.

## Test Plan

- [x] `test_invalid_max_patches_rejected` -- `20000`, nested `images_kwargs`, `0`, negative, above-limit, `bool`, `str`, and `float` raise `VLLMValidationError`.
- [x] `test_valid_max_patches_accepted` -- missing key, `1`, equal to the limit, and nested in-range values are accepted.
- [x] `test_non_mapping_mm_kwargs_rejected` -- a non-mapping kwargs object is rejected.
- [x] `test_get_hf_processor_rejects_oversized_max_patches` -- oversized kwargs never reach HF processor construction.
- [x] `test_get_num_patches_rejects_oversized_max_patches` -- HF `get_number_of_image_patches` is not called for oversized or nested oversized values.
- [x] `test_get_num_patches_forwards_in_range_max_patches` -- an in-range override is forwarded.
- [x] `test_operator_max_patches_is_the_request_cap` -- a server-configured cap is honored; values above it are rejected.
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass.

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)
