## Purpose

Follow-up to #57456. The `sm120` family of `_BATCH_INVARIANT_MATMUL_TUNED_CONFIGS` only covered the TP=1 shapes of Qwen3-1.7B / 4B / 8B, so with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `tensor_parallel_size > 1` every linear layer on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 50 still ran the batch-invariant persistent matmul with the default `128x128x64 / 8 warps / 3 stages` config (the TP=2 rows in #57456's comments show the resulting ~2.9x BI overhead unchanged by the table). Now that #57586 selects the tile config from the runtime M, the table is the remaining lever for TP.

This PR adds the 41 per-rank `(N, K)` shapes of the same three models at TP=2 / 4 / 8 (`qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` and the vocab-parallel `lm_head`; `(3072, 4096)` is shared by Qwen3-8B TP=2 qkv_proj and TP=8 gate_up_proj), 15 -> 56 entries. title: [Perf][MRV2] Allow FULL decode graphs for one-token prompt tails
body:
A one-token prompt tail over existing context runs exactly like a decode. This covers a full prefix-cache hit, a P/D KV import on the decode node, and a final one-token chunk. The scheduler may also pad such a tail with placeholder drafts to the K+1 spec-decode shape. The Mamba, GDN and KDA metadata builders already classify these rows as decodes.

Since #51865, any prefilling row made MRV2 reject the FULL decode graph for the whole batch. In P/D serving, every newly arriving request therefore pushed its step's decode batch down to PIECEWISE.

Classify graph eligibility from request state instead: a batch is eligible if every prefilling row schedules exactly one new prompt token (not counting drafts) over existing context. Fresh prompts and multi-token chunks are still excluded, so #49918 stays fixed. PCP batches keep the old behaviour.

- Add a decode_graph_eligible field on BatchReqState/InputBatch, computed in gather_batch_req_state. get_uniform_decode_token_count now takes decode_graph_eligible in place of has_prefill.
- The autoregressive and multi-module MTP drafters use the same flag, so they match the target model's graph mode.
- Compute the per-request draft counts once in gather_batch_req_state and reuse them in prepare_inputs.

This is an alternative / more general fix to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58374.

Note there is still an issue with hybrid models without this additional fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58434.

Used Opus 5.5 to help with this.

title: [ROCm][Perf] MXFP8 GEMM on native 32x32 block scales for gfx950
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek V4/V4.1 checkpoints store MXFP8 weight scales in 32x32 blocks. The
ModelOpt loader expands them to one scale row per weight row, and on gfx950
`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` then runs one generic `tl.dot_scaled`
kernel on those per-row scales. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash these linears
(`fused_wqa_wkv`, `wq_b`, the indexer `wq_b`, `wo_b`, and the shared-expert
`gate_up` and `down`) make up 11.7% of GPU kernel time per decode step at
TP2 conc32.

This PR keeps the checkpoint's 32x32 scale blocks and adds a GEMM that reads
them directly, tuned per shape for the V4.1-Flash projections. It is 1.49x
faster than the current kernel at the median, and 1.07x faster than the
native group32 GEMM in ROCm/aiter#5750 (latest head). End to end, over a
1-hour InferenceX agentx run (TP2, conc 32, DSpark x5), TPOT is 4.8% lower.

## What changes

- **`rocm_block32_gemm.py` (new):** a `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM for an MXFP8
  activation times an e4m3 weight with `[N/32, K/32]` E8M0 block scales.
  - A tiled kernel for larger M.
  - A packed kernel for small M. It fills the MFMA's rows with K panels
    instead of tokens and keeps only the matching-panel (block-diagonal)
    products, so a handful of tokens still streams the weight at full width.
  - Either kernel can split K. Normally the last program of each output tile
    sums the partials in split order within the same launch, so the result
    is deterministic and needs no second launch. A tile's splits run on one
    XCD, so they meet in its L2. The arrival counters are kept per stream.
    If a stream's first split-K launch happens inside a graph capture, it
    has no counters yet and uses a second reduce launch instead.
  - N and K are `constexpr` and M is runtime (`do_not_specialize`), so
    serving does not recompile per batch size.
  - The tile, split-K, MFMA shape and occupancy come from a table tuned on
    MI355X for the ten V4.1-Flash projections at TP2/TP4. Untuned shapes
    use a generic default.
  - It is registered as a custom op, because the config choice branches on
    M and the linear runs under `torch.compile`.
- **`RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`:**
  - `process_weights_after_loading` recovers the `[N/32, K/32]` blocks when
    every 32 rows share their scales, which is exactly what the loader
    produces from a 32x32 checkpoint.
  - `apply_weights` dispatches on the scale shape, so pre-processed
    (IPC-cached) weights work either way.
  - The block-scaled path also runs `K % 32 == 0` natively. DeepSeek-V4.1's
    shared-expert `down` at TP4 (K=576) was dequantized to BF16 at load
    before.
  - Checkpoints with per-row (1x32) scales keep the existing kernel
    unchanged.
- **Grouped MXFP8 `wo_a` GEMM (#58456):** `wo_a` goes through the same
  linear kernel, so its scales are now compact too. The kernel derives the
  scale row block from the scale shape and reads either layout.

## Kernel performance (MI355X, gfx950)

The numbers go through the vLLM entry point (custom op plus table lookup).
Weights are cold (rotated past the 256 MB MALL), timing uses HIP graphs,
and every arm gets identical MXFP8 inputs. All three kernels ran in one
session.

**Current kernel -> this PR**, in µs:

| fused wq_a\|wkv (1792x5120) | 7.2 -> 4.9 (1.47x) | 7.3 -> 5.6 (1.31x) | 9.0 -> 6.7 (1.35x) | 17.8 -> 7.8 (2.27x) | 17.8 -> 9.8 (1.82x) | 18.1 -> 10.0 (1.81x) | 27.2 -> 14.6 (1.87x) | 27.2 -> 22.7 (1.20x) | 33.1 -> 31.3 (1.06x) |

title: [Bugfix] DiffusionGemma: `diffusion_samples` to fan one seeded canvas out into n noise draws
body:
## Purpose

The current `structured_diffusion.py` server sends four identical requests in sampling mode and this works only because the engine itself is non-deterministic. If the upstream kernels end up becoming deterministic, the sampler will silently degrade.

How it works now: the current approach to sampling requires 1+N requests in auto mode (N=3), and N requests when explicitly specified. We can instead dispatch N requests in the server which can skip extra tokenization, prefix lookup, etc and individual response serialization. Then, the pinned positions are the noise template for multiple requests, and the children come back as k choices of one response.

The random draws are reproducible: a request seed reaches the children as seed + index, as it does for n, and a child with a seed draws its noise from a generator seeded with it.

The example structured server sends a fixed sample count this way with the schema seed, and keeps the auto policy on separate requests; --no-engine-samples restores the old behaviour for comparison. The diagnostics report the number of upstream requests beside the number of reads.

## Test Plan

Run the existing `structured_server.py`, test performance of "auto" and explicit "N" samples parameters.

## Test Results

With no additional load, timing is identical as requests are scheduled in parallel:

| test | time |
|--|--|
| 1 draw, cold prefix	| 112 ms |
| 4 draws as 4 concurrent requests, warm prefix	| 143 ms |
| 4 draws as one request, warm prefix	| 144 ms |
| 4 draws as 4 requests, cold prefix	| 188 ms |
| 4 draws as one request, cold prefix	| 187 ms |

This yields _slightly_ higher throughput near max server concurrency:

```
32 requests x 4 draws (diffusion_samples)    wall median   1215 ms (rounds [1298, 1215, 1174])  per-request median   765 ms  p90  1202 ms    26.3 answers/s   105.3 draws/s
128 requests x 1 draw (32 prompts x 4)       wall median   1292 ms (rounds [1314, 1217, 1292])  per-request median   785 ms  p90  1249 ms    24.8 answers/s    99.0 draws/s
```

title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Move remote region alignment into nixl utils
body:
## Purpose

**Stacked on #50499; land after it.** Both target `main`, so GitHub also lists #50499's commits. The change here is the last commit: [`488e5f7d6a...bab44092cf`](https://github.com/zixi-qi/vllm/compare/488e5f7d6af2819db8abf1fb74de06ed621b1cd6...bab44092cfd90b3f3cdd4bf8b462cca64dee3a72) (4 files, +143/−125).

Follows up on a [review note on #50499](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50499#discussion_r4098037609): `_align_remote_regions_by_layer` only transforms the remote `NixlAgentMetadata`, so it does not need to live on the worker.

- Move it to `nixl/utils.py` as `align_remote_regions_by_layer(meta, layer_names, local_region_indices, local_block_lens)`. It read exactly those three pieces of worker state, which are now passed explicitly.
- Add `select_remote_regions(meta, indices)`, which reindexes every per-region metadata list in one pass. Layer routing and the existing PP layer-window slice in `add_remote_agent` both use it, replacing two hand-written copies of the same seven-field reindexing.
- The packed-layout loop iterates `zip(..., strict=True)` instead of indexing three sequences by position.

No wire-format, registration, or transfer change; the validation checks and their messages are unchanged. One tightening: the PP layer-window slice now fails with "Remote region metadata lengths disagree" when a peer's per-region list length differs from its address list, where it previously truncated silently. Real peers always send equal lengths, since `register_kv_caches` asserts it.

Not a duplicate: no open PR moves or rewrites this function. Draft #56187 also builds on #50499 and changes this function under its earlier name; whichever lands second rebases onto the other.

## Test plan

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5700 \

Existing alignment tests now call the utility through a small `_align` helper; one new test covers the tightened length check, including that a rejected peer's metadata is left unmodified.

No model evaluation: the change moves code without changing registration or transfers. The E2E evidence for the packed MLA path (Gemma-4 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GSM8K) is in #50499.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Support bare call: and whitespace-free channel transitions in Gemma4 parser
body:
## Summary

Fixes #54256.

When serving Gemma-4 with reasoning and tool calling, the model frequently transitions directly out of reasoning (`<channel|>`) into emitting a tool call (`call:func{...}`) without re-emitting the optional `<|tool_call>` prefix. 

This PR ensures the Gemma4 parser handles bare `call:` transitions from both `CONTENT` and `REASONING` states, and fixes the offline fallback regex in `gemma4_utils.py` when `<channel|>` directly precedes `call:` without whitespace.

## Root Cause

1. In `vllm/parser/gemma4.py`, transitioning from `REASONING` to `CONTENT` on `THINK_END` left the FSM without a transition on `CALL_PREFIX` (`"call:"`). When the model dropped `<|tool_call>`, the tool call was silently dropped.
2. In `vllm/tool_parsers/gemma4_utils.py`, the fallback regex `r"(?:<call>|(?:^|\s)call:)(\w+)\{(.*?)\}"` required whitespace before `call:`, missing attached delimiters like `<channel|>call:...`.
3. Related to #53444 (which added `:` opener handling within `TOOL_PREAMBLE`, but still required `<|tool_call>` to reach `TOOL_PREAMBLE`) and #53363 / #53255 (empty `tool_calls` with `finish_reason="tool_calls"`).

## Fix

1. **`vllm/parser/gemma4.py`**:
   - Added `(ParserState.CONTENT, "CALL_PREFIX") -> ParserState.TOOL_NAME` transition emitting `EventType.TOOL_CALL_START`.
   - Added `(ParserState.REASONING, "CALL_PREFIX") -> ParserState.TOOL_NAME` transition emitting `(EventType.REASONING_END, EventType.TOOL_CALL_START)`.
2. **`vllm/tool_parsers/gemma4_utils.py`**:
   - Updated fallback pattern to `r"(?:<call>|(?:^|\s|<channel\|>|:)call:)([\w\-\.]+)\{(.*?)\}"`.
3. **Tests** (`tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_regex_and_bare_calls.py`):
   - Exercises the production `vllm.tool_parsers.gemma4_utils.parse_tool_calls` directly (no copied local regex constants), so regressions in the real tiered pattern are caught. Cases assert both the parsed function name and arguments:
     - Tier 1: canonical tag-wrapped calls, `<turn|>` closure, multiple sequential calls, `strict=True` ignoring fallback shapes
     - Tier 2: bare `call:` glued to `<channel|>` (no whitespace), colon-prefixed `<|tool_call>:call:...`, leading-whitespace bare call, fragmented `<call>` tag, hyphen- and dot-containing tool names, no-call -> empty
   - Retains the `Gemma4EngineToolParser` + offline `parse_tool_calls` integration cases.

## Verification

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_regex_and_bare_calls.py tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py
```
- 67/67 tests pass (13 in `test_gemma4_regex_and_bare_calls.py` + 54 existing).
- Verified against live Blackwell GPU deployment.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to refactor the regression tests to exercise the production parser. All changes were reviewed line-by-line by the submitter.

title: [MRV2] Minor model_runner.py code cleanup
[Perf] DiffusionGemma: one-pass sampler statistics kernel
body:
## Purpose

Followup to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250 - helps decoding for diffusiongemma in both text and structured answer mode (the latter only at high concurrency, the former in all cases I've found).

A custom diffusiongemma Triton kernel: 

 - one program per logits row
 - does an online max and sum in one pass
 - draws Gumbel noise inline from Philox instead of materializing a noise tensor
 - writes the softmax once in the embedding dtype (only when self-conditioning will read it)

Replaces _compiled_sample_step's older process which was several fused kernels that performed:

 - Cast the logits to fp32 and divide every element by the request's temperature.
 - Draw a uniform random tensor the same size as the logits, turn it into Gumbel noise with two logs, add it to the scaled logits, and take the argmax of that for the sample.
 - Take the argmax of the scaled logits themselves for the committed token.
 - Compute log_softmax over each row, exponentiate it to get the probabilities, multiply the two and sum for the entropy.
 - Cast the probabilities to bf16 for the self-conditioning matmul.

(each of those is at least one read and often one write of a [4096, 262144] fp32 tensor at concurrency 32)

## Test Plan

title: [ROCm][Perf] Kimi-K3 Enable sharded latent MoE up-projection under EP
body: ## Purpose `ROCmLatentMoERunner` has a column-parallel tail that splits the routed-expert up-projection across ranks and accumulates each rank's shard into its slice of the shared-expert output with `addmm_`, so the shared+routed combine costs no extra kernel. It was gated on `moe_config.tp_size > 1`, which vLLM sets to `1` under expert parallelism, so under `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel` the tail has never run: every rank computed the full 3584 -> 7168 projection and then added the shared output in a separate elementwise kernel. `moe_config.tp_size` describes how the *experts* are split. How many ranks share the hidden dimension is a different question, and its answer is the TP process group world size — which is also the group that `get_tensor_model_parallel_rank()` indexes and that `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` reduces over. This derives the gate and the shard size from that world size instead. `_shard_up_proj_tail` needs no change; it already indexes with the TP rank, which is now consistent with the shard size. The arithmetic is unchanged and holds under EP: the latent is all-reduced before the up-projection so its input is replicated, `shared_output` is still an unreduced TP partial because the dense layers and the shared expert stay at TP=8, and the final all-reduce still fires (`ep_size > 1`). Before: After: This also fixes two configurations that were silently wrong before, because `moe_config.tp_size` is flattened across DP without EP while the TP group is not: | config | `moe.tp_size` | TP world | before | after | |---|---|---|---|---| | TP=8 | 8 | 8 | shards correctly | unchanged | | TP=8 + EP | 1 | 8 | replicated (this bug) | shards correctly | | TP=2 x DP=2 | 4 | 2 | shards by 4, covers half the hidden dim | shards correctly | | DP=4, TP=1 | 4 | 1 | shards by 4 with no group to reduce over | replicated | ## Test Plan `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_latent_moe_runner.py` on 8x MI325X. The existing TP4/TP8 tests that assert the sharded tail equals the replicated projection are unchanged — a wrong shard offset or a dropped accumulation still runs and still produces plausible text. Added: - `test_shards_under_the_kimi_k3_serving_config_with_expert_parallel` — the gate regression this PR fixes. Fails before the change. - `test_sharded_tail_tp8_ep8_matches_replicated_projection` — the real distributed path at TP8 with an EP-shaped MoE config, so the final reduce is exercised rather than assumed. - `test_shards_by_the_process_group_not_the_dp_flattened_tp_size` and a `dp-without-tp` fallback case for the two DP rows above. - The `no-tp` fallback case became a genuine single-rank case, since `moe_config.tp_size == 1` no longer means "there is no tensor parallelism". ## Test Results 18 passed. Startup now logs the sharded-tail `info_once` and not the fallback `warning_once`. gsm8k on MI325X: local-completions ({'model': 'kimi-k3', 'base_url': 'http://localhost:8000/v1/completions', 'num_concurrent': 32, 'max_retries': 10, 'max_gen_toks': 2048, 'tokenizer_backend': 'None', 'tokenized_requests': 'False'}), gen_kwargs: ({}), limit: None, num_fewshot: 5, batch_size: auto |Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr| |-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:| |gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9598|±  |0.0054| |     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9598|±  |0.0054| **128K ISL / 1K OSL** on MI325X, TP8 + EP, before vs after: | concurrency | TTFT | TPOT | output tok/s | |---|---|---|---| | 2 | −3.2% (28.92 → 28.01 s) | −5.2% (51.81 → 49.10 ms) | +4.2% | | 4 | −2.4% (31.54 → 30.80 s) | −4.8% (100.30 → 95.53 ms) | +4.3% | | 6 | −2.2% (30.69 → 30.00 s) | −3.8% (153.62 → 147.71 ms) | +3.8% | | 8 | −0.8% (30.12 → 29.89 s) | −3.9% (202.74 → 194.93 ms) | +3.7% | This PR was made with help of AI.
